1.m: We shall explain the measurement and sacrificial enclosure layouts of their ground.

1.s: athāṅgulapramāṇaṃ caturdaśāṇavaḥ catustriṃśattilāḥ pṛthusaṃśliṣṭā ityaparam | daśāṅgulaṃ kṣudrapadam | dvādaśa prādeśaḥ | pṛthottarayuge trayodaśike | padaṃ pañcadaśa | aṣṭāśītiśatamīṣā | catuḥśatamakṣaḥ | ṣaḍaśītiryugam | dvātriṃśajjānuḥ | ṣaṭtriṃśacchamyābāhū | dvipadaḥ prakramaḥ | dvau prādeśāvaratniḥ | athāpyudāharanti pade yuge prakrame 'ratnāviyati śamyāyāṃ ca mānārtheṣu yāthākāmīti | pañcāratniḥ puruṣo vyāmaśca | caturaratnirvyāyāmaḥ ||
1.d: अथाङ्गुलप्रमाणं चतुर्दशाणवः चतुस्त्रिंशत्तिलाः पृथुसंश्लिष्टा इत्यपरम् । दशाङ्गुलं क्षुद्रपदम् । द्वादश प्रादेशः । पृथोत्तरयुगे त्रयोदशिके । पदं पञ्चदश । अष्टाशीतिशतमीषा । चतुःशतमक्षः । षडशीतिर्युगम् । द्वात्रिंशज्जानुः । षट्त्रिंशच्छम्याबाहू । द्विपदः प्रक्रमः । द्वौ प्रादेशावरत्निः । अथाप्युदाहरन्ति पदे युगे प्रक्रमे ऽरत्नावियति शम्यायां च मानार्थेषु याथाकामीति । पञ्चारत्निः पुरुषो व्यामश्च । चतुररत्निर्व्यायामः ॥
1.m: Now, the standard measure of a finger-breadth: fourteen minute grains; or according to another [view], thirty-four sesame seeds placed broadside against one another. / A short foot is ten finger-breadths. / A span is twelve. / In the broad and north-facing yoke [it is] thirteen. / A foot is fifteen. / A chariot pole is one hundred and eighty-eight. / An axle is one hundred and four. / A yoke is eighty-six. / A knee is thirty-two. / A yoke-pin and a short arm are thirty-six. / A stride is two feet. / Two spans are a cubit. / Moreover, they quote: in the foot, the yoke, the stride, the cubit, the fathom, and the yoke-pin, one may act according to pleasure regarding measures. / A man's height is five cubits, and [so is] a fathom. / An extended arm-span is four cubits.

1.s: caturaśraṃ cikīrṣanyāvaccikīrṣettāvatīṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | lekhāmālikhya tasyā madhye śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | tasminpāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet | viṣkambhāntayoḥ śaṅkū nihanyāt | pūrvasminpāśaṃ pratimucya pāśena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet | evamaparasmiṃste yatra sameyātāṃ tena dvitīyaṃ viṣkambhamāyacchet | viṣkambhāntayoḥ śaṅkū nihanyāt | pūrvasminpāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet | evaṃ dakṣiṇata evaṃ paścādevamuttaratasteṣāṃ ye 'ntyāḥ saṃsargāstaccaturaśraṃ saṃpadyate ||
1.d: चतुरश्रं चिकीर्षन्यावच्चिकीर्षेत्तावतीं रज्जुमुभयतः पाशां कृत्वा मध्ये लक्षणं करोति । लेखामालिख्य तस्या मध्ये शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । तस्मिन्पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन मण्डलं परिलिखेत् । विष्कम्भान्तयोः शङ्कू निहन्यात् । पूर्वस्मिन्पाशं प्रतिमुच्य पाशेन मण्डलं परिलिखेत् । एवमपरस्मिंस्ते यत्र समेयातां तेन द्वितीयं विष्कम्भमायच्छेत् । विष्कम्भान्तयोः शङ्कू निहन्यात् । पूर्वस्मिन्पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन मण्डलं परिलिखेत् । एवं दक्षिणत एवं पश्चादेवमुत्तरतस्तेषां ये ऽन्त्याः संसर्गास्तच्चतुरश्रं संपद्यते ॥
1.m: Wishing to make a four-sided figure: as large as one wishes to make it, having made a measuring cord of that length with a loop at both ends, one makes a mark in the middle. / Having drawn a line, one should drive in a gnomon peg in its middle. / Having fastened the two loops on it, one should scribe a circle with the mark. / One should drive in gnomon pegs at the two ends of the diameter. / Having fastened a loop on the eastern one, one should scribe a circle with the loop. / In the same way on the western one. Where the two [circles] meet, by that [line] one should stretch the second diameter. / One should drive in gnomon pegs at the two ends of the diameter. / Having fastened the two loops on the eastern one, one should scribe a circle with the mark. / Thus on the south, thus on the west, thus on the north. Their outer intersections—that four-sided figure is produced.

1.s: athāparam | pramāṇāddviguṇāṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | sa prācyarthaḥ | aparasminnardhe caturbhāgone lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | tannyañcanam | ardheṃ 'sārthaṃ | pṛṣṭhyāntayaoḥ pāśau pratimucya nyañcanena dakṣiṇāpāyamyārdhena śroṇyaṃsānnirharet ||
1.d: अथापरम् । प्रमाणाद्द्विगुणां रज्जुमुभयतः पाशां कृत्वा मध्ये लक्षणं करोति । स प्राच्यर्थः । अपरस्मिन्नर्धे चतुर्भागोने लक्षणं करोति । तन्न्यञ्चनम् । अर्धें ऽसार्थं । पृष्ठ्यान्तयओः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य न्यञ्चनेन दक्षिणापायम्यार्धेन श्रोण्यंसान्निर्हरेत् ॥
1.m: Now another [method]. Having made a measuring cord twice the standard measure with a loop at both ends, one makes a mark in the middle. / That is for the eastern [half]. / In the other half, one makes a mark lessened by a fourth part. / That is the inner mark. / In the [remaining] half [there is a mark] for the shoulders. / Having fastened the two loops at the two ends of the spine, having drawn [the cord] out to the south by the inner mark, one should fix the hips and the shoulders by the [other] half.

1.s: dīrghacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣanyāvaccikīrṣe ttāvatyāṃ bhūmyāṃ dvau śaṅkū nihanyāt | dvau dvāvekaikamabhitaḥ samau | yāvatī tiryaṅmānī tāvatīṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | pūrveṣāmantyayoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | madhyame pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇasyopariṣṭāddakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | soṃ 'sa etenottaroṃ 'so vyākhyātastathā śroṇī ||
1.d: दीर्घचतुरश्रं चिकीर्षन्यावच्चिकीर्षे त्तावत्यां भूम्यां द्वौ शङ्कू निहन्यात् । द्वौ द्वावेकैकमभितः समौ । यावती तिर्यङ्मानी तावतीं रज्जुमुभयतः पाशां कृत्वा मध्ये लक्षणं करोति । पूर्वेषामन्त्ययोः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणापायम्य लक्षणे लक्षणं करोति । मध्यमे पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणस्योपरिष्टाद्दक्षिणापायम्य लक्षणे शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । सों ऽस एतेनोत्तरों ऽसो व्याख्यातस्तथा श्रोणी ॥
1.m: Wishing to make an oblong: on ground as large as one wishes to make it, one should drive in two gnomon pegs. / Two on each side, equal to one another. / As long as the transverse-measuring side is, having made a measuring cord of that length with a loop at both ends, one makes a mark in the middle. / Having fastened the two loops to the outer [pegs] of the eastern ones, having drawn [the cord] out to the south by the mark, one makes a mark at the mark. / Having fastened the two loops to the middle one, having drawn [the cord] out to the south above the mark, one should drive in a gnomon peg at the mark. / That is the shoulder. By this the northern shoulder is explained, likewise the hip.

1.s: yatra purastādaṃhīyasīṃ minuyāttatra tadardhe lakṣaṇaṃ karoti ||
1.d: यत्र पुरस्तादंहीयसीं मिनुयात्तत्र तदर्धे लक्षणं करोति ॥
1.m: Where one would measure a narrower [side] in front, there one makes a mark at its half.

1.s: athāparam | pramāṇādadhyardhāṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvāparasmiṃstṛtīye ṣaḍbhāgone lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | tannyañchanam | iṣṭeṃ 'sārtham | pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ pāśau pratimucya nyañchanena dakṣiṇāpāyamyeṣṭena śroṇyaṃsānnirharet ||
1.d: अथापरम् । प्रमाणादध्यर्धां रज्जुमुभयतः पाशां कृत्वापरस्मिंस्तृतीये षड्भागोने लक्षणं करोति । तन्न्यञ्छनम् । इष्टें ऽसार्थम् । पृष्ठ्यान्तयोः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य न्यञ्छनेन दक्षिणापायम्येष्टेन श्रोण्यंसान्निर्हरेत् ॥
1.m: Now another [method]. Having made a measuring cord one and a half times the standard measure with a loop at both ends, one makes a mark in the other third, lessened by a sixth part. / That is the inner mark. / [A mark is made at the point] desired for the shoulders. / Having fastened the two loops at the two ends of the spine, having drawn [the cord] out to the south by the inner mark, one should fix the hips and the shoulders by the desired [mark].
The diagonal cord of an equilateral four-sided figure produces an area twice as large.
The transverse [side] is the standard measure; the length is the cord producing a square of double area; its diagonal cord is the cord producing a square of triple area.
By this the cord producing a square of one-third area is explained; but the area becomes a ninth part [of the square of triple area].

1.s: dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pārśvamānī tiryaṅmānī ca yatpṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṃ karoti ||
1.d: दीर्घचतुरश्रस्याक्ष्णयारज्जुः पार्श्वमानी तिर्यङ्मानी च यत्पृथग्भूते कुरुतस्तदुभयं करोति ॥
1.m: The diagonal cord of an oblong produces both [areas] that the flank-measuring side and the transverse-measuring side produce separately.

Among them, [this is] observed in [rectangles with sides of] three and four, of twelve and five, of fifteen and eight, of seven and twenty-four, of twelve and thirty-five, and of fifteen and thirty-six.

2.s: nānācaturaśre samasyankanīyasaḥ karaṇyā varṣīyaso vṛdhramullikhet | vṛdhrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ samastayoḥ pārśvamānī bhavati ||
2.d: नानाचतुरश्रे समस्यन्कनीयसः करण्या वर्षीयसो वृध्रमुल्लिखेत् । वृध्रस्याक्ष्णयारज्जुः समस्तयोः पार्श्वमानी भवति ॥
2.m: When combining different four-sided figures, one should cut off a strip segment of the larger with the producing side of the smaller. / The diagonal cord of the strip segment becomes the flank-measuring side of both combined.

2.s: caturaśrāccaturaśraṃ nirjihīrṣanyāvannirjihīrṣettasya karaṇyā varṣīyaso vṛdhramullikhet | vṛdhrasya pārśvamānīmakṣṇayetaratpārśvamupasaṃharet | sā yatra nipatettadapacchindyāt | chinnayā nirastam ||
2.d: चतुरश्राच्चतुरश्रं निर्जिहीर्षन्यावन्निर्जिहीर्षेत्तस्य करण्या वर्षीयसो वृध्रमुल्लिखेत् । वृध्रस्य पार्श्वमानीमक्ष्णयेतरत्पार्श्वमुपसंहरेत् । सा यत्र निपतेत्तदपच्छिन्द्यात् । छिन्नया निरस्तम् ॥
2.m: Wishing to subtract a four-sided figure from a four-sided figure: as much as one wishes to subtract, with its producing side one should cut off a strip segment of the larger. / One should turn the flank-measuring side of the strip segment diagonally to the other flank. / Where it falls, there one should cut off. / By the [part] cut off, [the required figure] is removed.

2.s: samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣaṃstadakṣṇayāpacchidya bhāgaṃ dvedhā vibhajya pārśvayorupadadhyādyathāyogam ||
2.d: समचतुरश्रं दीर्घचतुरश्रं चिकीर्षंस्तदक्ष्णयापच्छिद्य भागं द्वेधा विभज्य पार्श्वयोरुपदध्याद्यथायोगम् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make an equilateral four-sided figure into an oblong: having cut it across diagonally, having divided that portion into two, one should place [them] on the two flanks as fitting.

2.s: api vai tasmiṃścaturaśraṃ samasya tasya karaṇyāpacchidya yadatiśiṣyate taditaratropadadhyāt ||
2.d: अपि वै तस्मिंश्चतुरश्रं समस्य तस्य करण्यापच्छिद्य यदतिशिष्यते तदितरत्रोपदध्यात् ॥
2.m: Or indeed, having combined a four-sided figure onto it, having cut off with its producing side, that which remains over one should place on the other side.

2.s: dīrghacaturaśraṃ samacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣaṃstiryaṅmānīṃ karaṇīṃ kṛtvā śeṣaṃ dvedhā vibhajya pārśvayorupadadhyāt | khaṇḍamāvāpena tatsaṃpūrayet | tasya nirhāra uktaḥ ||
2.d: दीर्घचतुरश्रं समचतुरश्रं चिकीर्षंस्तिर्यङ्मानीं करणीं कृत्वा शेषं द्वेधा विभज्य पार्श्वयोरुपदध्यात् । खण्डमावापेन तत्संपूरयेत् । तस्य निर्हार उक्तः ॥
2.m: Wishing to make an oblong into an equilateral four-sided figure: having made the transverse-measuring side the producing side, having divided the remainder into two, one should place [them] on the two flanks. / One should fill up the corner piece by an insertion. / Its removal has [already] been stated.

2.s: caturaśramekato 'ṇimaccikīrṣannaṇimataḥ karaṇīṃ tiryaṅmānīṃ kṛtvā śeṣamakṣṇayā vibhajya viparyasyetaratropadadhyāt ||
2.d: चतुरश्रमेकतो ऽणिमच्चिकीर्षन्नणिमतः करणीं तिर्यङ्मानीं कृत्वा शेषमक्ष्णया विभज्य विपर्यस्येतरत्रोपदध्यात् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make a four-sided figure narrower on one side: having made the producing side of the narrower [side] the transverse-measuring side, having divided the remainder diagonally, having inverted [it], one should place [it] on the other side.

2.s: caturaśraṃ praugaṃ cikīrṣanyāvaccikīrṣeddvistāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ samacaturaśrāṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyāḥ madhye śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | tasminpāśau pratimucya dakṣiṇottarayoḥ śroṇyornipātayet | bahispandyamapacchindyāt ||
2.d: चतुरश्रं प्रौगं चिकीर्षन्यावच्चिकीर्षेद्द्विस्तावतीं भूमिं समचतुरश्रां कृत्वा पूर्वस्याः करण्याः मध्ये शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । तस्मिन्पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य दक्षिणोत्तरयोः श्रोण्योर्निपातयेत् । बहिस्पन्द्यमपच्छिन्द्यात् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make a four-sided figure into an equilateral triangle: as large as one wishes to make it, having made ground twice as large into an equilateral four-sided figure, one should drive in a gnomon peg in the middle of the eastern producing side. / Having fastened the two loops on it, one should drop [the cords] to the southern and northern hips. / One should cut away what is outside the cord.

2.s: caturaśramubhayataḥ praugaṃ cikīrṣanyāvaccikīrṣeddvistāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ dīrghacaturaśrāṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyāḥ madhye śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | tasminpāśau pratimucya dakṣiṇottarayormadhyadeśayornipātayet | bahiḥspandyamapacchindyāt | etenāparaṃ praugaṃ vyākhyātam ||
2.d: चतुरश्रमुभयतः प्रौगं चिकीर्षन्यावच्चिकीर्षेद्द्विस्तावतीं भूमिं दीर्घचतुरश्रां कृत्वा पूर्वस्याः करण्याः मध्ये शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । तस्मिन्पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य दक्षिणोत्तरयोर्मध्यदेशयोर्निपातयेत् । बहिःस्पन्द्यमपच्छिन्द्यात् । एतेनापरं प्रौगं व्याख्यातम् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make a four-sided figure into a rhombus: as large as one wishes to make it, having made ground twice as large into an oblong, one should drive in a gnomon peg in the middle of the eastern producing side. / Having fastened the two loops on it, one should drop [the cords] to the southern and northern middle points. / One should cut away what is outside the cord. By this the western equilateral triangle is explained.

2.s: caturaśraṃ maṇḍalaṃ cikīrṣannakṣṇayārdhaṃ madhyātprācīmabhyāpātayet | yadatiśiṣyate tasya saha tṛtīyena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet ||
2.d: चतुरश्रं मण्डलं चिकीर्षन्नक्ष्णयार्धं मध्यात्प्राचीमभ्यापातयेत् । यदतिशिष्यते तस्य सह तृतीयेन मण्डलं परिलिखेत् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make a four-sided figure into a circle: one should drop half the diagonal from the center towards the east. / With what remains over together with a third [of it], one should scribe a circle.

2.s: maṇḍalaṃ caturaśraṃ cikīrṣanviṣkambhamaṣṭau bhāgānkṛtvā bhāgamekonatriṃśadhā vibhajyāṣṭāviṃśatibhāgānuddharet | bhāgasya ca ṣaṣṭhamaṣṭamabhāgonam ||
2.d: मण्डलं चतुरश्रं चिकीर्षन्विष्कम्भमष्टौ भागान्कृत्वा भागमेकोनत्रिंशधा विभज्याष्टाविंशतिभागानुद्धरेत् । भागस्य च षष्ठमष्टमभागोनम् ॥
2.m: Wishing to make a circle into a four-sided figure: having made the diameter into eight parts, having divided one part into twenty-nine, one should remove twenty-eight parts; / and a sixth of that part, lessened by an eighth part.

2.s: api vā pañcadaśabhāgānkṛtvā dvāvuddharet | saiṣānityā caturaśrakaraṇī ||
2.d: अपि वा पञ्चदशभागान्कृत्वा द्वावुद्धरेत् । सैषानित्या चतुरश्रकरणी ॥
2.m: Or having made [the diameter] into fifteen parts, one should remove two. / This is the transient producing side of the four-sided figure.
One should increase the standard measure by its third, and that by its fourth, less a thirty-fourth of itself. / [This is] the diagonal with its specific excess.

3.s: athāgnyādheyike vihāre gārhapatyādāhavanīyasyāyatanam | vijñāyate 'ṣṭaṣu prakrameṣu brāhmaṇo 'gnimādadhītaikādaśasu rājanyo dvādaśasu vaiśya iti ||
3.d: अथाग्न्याधेयिके विहारे गार्हपत्यादाहवनीयस्यायतनम् । विज्ञायते ऽष्टषु प्रक्रमेषु ब्राह्मणो ऽग्निमादधीतैकादशसु राजन्यो द्वादशसु वैश्य इति ॥
3.m: Now in the sacrificial enclosure layout for the establishment of the fires, the position of the offering fire altar from the householder's hearth-fire: / it is known [from sacred tradition]: 'At eight strides a brāhmaṇa should establish the fire, at eleven a rājanya, at twelve a vaiśya.'

3.s: āyāmatṛtīyena trīṇi caturaśrāṇyanūcīnāni kārayet | aparasyottarasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ gārhapatyaḥ | tasyaiva dakṣiṇeṃ 'se 'nvāhāryapacanaḥ pūrvasyottareṃ 'sa āhavanīyaḥ ||
3.d: आयामतृतीयेन त्रीणि चतुरश्राण्यनूचीनानि कारयेत् । अपरस्योत्तरस्यां श्रोण्यां गार्हपत्यः । तस्यैव दक्षिणें ऽसे ऽन्वाहार्यपचनः पूर्वस्योत्तरें ऽस आहवनीयः ॥
3.m: With a third of the length, one should cause three four-sided figures to be made in a row. / On the northern hip of the western [one] is the householder's hearth-fire. / On the southern shoulder of that very same [figure] is the southern cooking-fire hearth; on the northern shoulder of the eastern [one] is the offering fire altar.

3.s: api vā gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālaṃ pañcadhā ṣoḍhā vā saṃbhujya ṣaṣṭhaṃ saptamaṃ vā bhāgamāgantukamupasamasya samaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya pūrvasmādantād dvayorbhāgayorlakṣaṇaṃ karoti | gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantau niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe śaṅkuṃ nihanti | taddakṣiṇāgnerāyatanaṃ bhavati ||
3.d: अपि वा गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरन्तरालं पञ्चधा षोढा वा संभुज्य षष्ठं सप्तमं वा भागमागन्तुकमुपसमस्य समं त्रैधं विभज्य पूर्वस्मादन्ताद् द्वयोर्भागयोर्लक्षणं करोति । गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरन्तौ नियम्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणापायम्य लक्षणे शङ्कुं निहन्ति । तद्दक्षिणाग्नेरायतनं भवति ॥
3.m: Or else, having folded the space between the gārhapatya and the āhavanīya into five or into six, having added an extra sixth or seventh part, [and] having divided it equally into three parts, one makes a mark at two parts from the eastern end. Having fastened the ends at the gārhapatya and the āhavanīya, having stretched [the cord] to the south by the mark, one drives a peg into the mark. That becomes the site of the dakṣiṇāgni.

3.s: api vā pramāṇaṃ pañcamena vardhayet | tatsarvaṃ pañcadhā saṃbhujyāparasmādantāddvayorbhāgayorlakṣaṇaṃ karoti | pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe śaṅkuṃ nihanti | taddakṣi ṇāgnerāyatanaṃ bhavati ||
3.d: अपि वा प्रमाणं पञ्चमेन वर्धयेत् । तत्सर्वं पञ्चधा संभुज्यापरस्मादन्ताद्द्वयोर्भागयोर्लक्षणं करोति । पृष्ठ्यान्तयोः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणापायम्य लक्षणे शङ्कुं निहन्ति । तद्दक्षि णाग्नेरायतनं भवति ॥
3.m: Or else, one should increase the standard measure by a fifth part. Having folded that whole [cord] into five, one makes a mark at two parts from the western end. Having fastened the loops to both ends of the spine, having stretched [the cord] to the south by the mark, one drives a peg into the mark. That becomes the site of the dakṣiṇāgni.
Reversed by this [same procedure], the rubbish-heap is explained.
To the west of the āhavanīya, it is as long as the sacrificer: thus it is known from tradition regarding the altar of the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

3.s: tasyāstribhāgonaṃ paścāttiraścī | tasyā evārdhaṃ purastāttiraścī | evaṃ dīrghacaturaśramekato 'ṇimadvihṛtya sraktiṣu śaṅkūnnihanyāt ||
3.d: तस्यास्त्रिभागोनं पश्चात्तिरश्ची । तस्या एवार्धं पुरस्तात्तिरश्ची । एवं दीर्घचतुरश्रमेकतो ऽणिमद्विहृत्य स्रक्तिषु शङ्कून्निहन्यात् ॥
3.m: Its transverse side at the back is reduced by a third part; its transverse side in front is half of that [length]. Having thus laid out an oblong tapering to one side, one should drive pegs into the corners.

3.s: yāvatī pārśvamānī dvirabhyastā tāvatīṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | dakṣiṇayoḥ pārśvayoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | tasminpāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ parilikhet | etenottaraṃ pārśvaṃ vyākhyātam | pūvaṃ pārśvaṃ tayā dvirabhyastayā parilikhet | evamaparam ||
3.d: यावती पार्श्वमानी द्विरभ्यस्ता तावतीं रज्जुमुभयतः पाशां कृत्वा मध्ये लक्षणं करोति । दक्षिणयोः पार्श्वयोः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणापायम्य लक्षणे शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । तस्मिन्पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणं पार्श्वं परिलिखेत् । एतेनोत्तरं पार्श्वं व्याख्यातम् । पूवं पार्श्वं तया द्विरभ्यस्तया परिलिखेत् । एवमपरम् ॥
3.m: Having made a cord as long as the flank-measuring side doubled, with loops at both ends, one makes a mark in the middle. Having fastened the loops to the two southern sides [corners], having stretched [the cord] to the south by the mark, one should drive a peg into the mark. Having fastened the loops to that [peg], one should circumscribe the southern side by the mark. By this the northern side is explained. One should circumscribe the eastern side with that [cord] doubled. Likewise the western.

3.s: daśapadā paścāttiraścī dvādaśapadā prācyaṣṭāpadā purastāttiraścīti pāśubandhikāyā vedervijñāyate | mānayogastasyā vyākhyātaḥ | rathasaṃmitetyekeṣām | virāṭsaṃpannetyekeṣām ||
3.d: दशपदा पश्चात्तिरश्ची द्वादशपदा प्राच्यष्टापदा पुरस्तात्तिरश्चीति पाशुबन्धिकाया वेदेर्विज्ञायते । मानयोगस्तस्या व्याख्यातः । रथसंमितेत्येकेषाम् । विराट्संपन्नेत्येकेषाम् ॥
3.m: Ten feet [is] the transverse side at the back, twelve feet the eastern [spine], eight feet the transverse side in front: thus it is known from tradition regarding the altar of the animal sacrifice. The application of measurement for it has been explained. According to some, it matches a chariot; according to some, it accomplishes the virāj.
It is four-cornered and the size of a yoke-pin: thus it is known from tradition regarding the high altar; because of not differing from a square.

3.s: vitṛtīyā vedirbhavatīti paitṛkyā vedervijñāyate | mahāvedestṛtīyena samacaturaśrakṛtāyāstṛtīyakaraṇī bhavatīti | navamastu bhūmerbhāgo bhavati | yajamānamātrī catuḥsraktirbhavatītyekeṣām | dikṣu sraktayo bhavanti ||
3.d: वितृतीया वेदिर्भवतीति पैतृक्या वेदेर्विज्ञायते । महावेदेस्तृतीयेन समचतुरश्रकृतायास्तृतीयकरणी भवतीति । नवमस्तु भूमेर्भागो भवति । यजमानमात्री चतुःस्रक्तिर्भवतीत्येकेषाम् । दिक्षु स्रक्तयो भवन्ति ॥
3.m: The altar is one-third: thus it is known from tradition regarding the ancestral altar. Of the great altar made into a square, by one-third it is a cord producing a square of one-third area; but it is a ninth part of the ground. According to some, it is the size of the sacrificer and four-cornered. Its corners are oriented to the cardinal directions.

3.s: veditṛtīye yajeteti sautrāmaṇikīṃ vedimabhyupadiśanti | mahāvedestṛtīyena samacaturaśrakṛtāyā aṣṭādaśapadā pārśvamānī bhavati | tasyai dīrghakaraṇyāmekato 'ṇimatkaraṇyāṃ ca yathākāmīti ||
3.d: वेदितृतीये यजेतेति सौत्रामणिकीं वेदिमभ्युपदिशन्ति । महावेदेस्तृतीयेन समचतुरश्रकृताया अष्टादशपदा पार्श्वमानी भवति । तस्यै दीर्घकरण्यामेकतो ऽणिमत्करण्यां च यथाकामीति ॥
3.m: One should sacrifice on a third of the altar: thus they teach concerning the Sautrāmaṇī altar. Of the great altar made into a square, by one-third its flank-measuring side is eighteen feet. One may, at wish, make it an oblong or taper it to one side.

4.s: prāgvaṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśaprakramāyāmo dvādaśavyāso 'pi vā dvādaśaprakramāyāmo daśavyāsaḥ ||
4.d: प्राग्वंशः षोडशप्रक्रमायामो द्वादशव्यासो ऽपि वा द्वादशप्रक्रमायामो दशव्यासः ॥
4.m: The east-facing shed has a length of sixteen strides and a width of twelve, or else a length of twelve strides and a width of ten.
In the middle of it is the sacrificial enclosure layout of twelve [strides].

4.s: triṃśatpadāni prakramā vā paścāttiraścī bhavati ṣaṭtriṃśatprācī caturviṃśatiḥ purastāttiraścīti mahāvedervijñāyate | mānayogastasyā vyākhyātaḥ | āhavanīyātṣaṭ prakramānmahāvediḥ ||
4.d: त्रिंशत्पदानि प्रक्रमा वा पश्चात्तिरश्ची भवति षट्त्रिंशत्प्राची चतुर्विंशतिः पुरस्तात्तिरश्चीति महावेदेर्विज्ञायते । मानयोगस्तस्या व्याख्यातः । आहवनीयात्षट् प्रक्रमान्महावेदिः ॥
4.m: Thirty feet or strides is the transverse side at the back, thirty-six the eastern [spine], twenty-four the transverse side in front: thus it is known from tradition regarding the great altar. The application of measurement for it has been explained. The great altar is six strides from the āhavanīya.

4.s: tata ekasminsadaḥ | taddaśakam | udak saptaviṃśatyaratnayaḥ | aṣṭādaśetyekeṣām ||
4.d: तत एकस्मिन्सदः । तद्दशकम् । उदक् सप्तविंशत्यरत्नयः । अष्टादशेत्येकेषाम् ॥
4.m: One [stride] from that is the sadas; that is of ten [strides]. Towards the north it is twenty-seven cubits; according to some, eighteen.

4.s: tataścaturṣu havirdhānam | taddaśakaṃ dvādaśakaṃ vā mānayogastayorvyākhyātaḥ ||
4.d: ततश्चतुर्षु हविर्धानम् । तद्दशकं द्वादशकं वा मानयोगस्तयोर्व्याख्यातः ॥
4.m: Four [strides] from that is the havirdhāna shed; that is of ten or twelve [strides]. The application of measurement for those two has been explained.

4.s: yūpāvaṭīyācchaṅkorardhaprakramamavaśiṣyottaravediṃ vimimīte | daśapadottaravedirbhavatīti some vijñāyate | mānayogastasyā vyākhyātaḥ ||
4.d: यूपावटीयाच्छङ्कोरर्धप्रक्रममवशिष्योत्तरवेदिं विमिमीते । दशपदोत्तरवेदिर्भवतीति सोमे विज्ञायते । मानयोगस्तस्या व्याख्यातः ॥
4.m: Leaving half a stride from the peg for the sacrificial post hole, one measures out the high altar. The high altar is of ten feet: thus it is known from tradition in the soma sacrifice. The application of measurement for it has been explained.
The pit is the size of a yoke-pin or unmeasured.

4.s: athoparavāḥ prādeśamukhāḥ prādeśāntarālāḥ | aratnimātraṃ samacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya sraktiṣu śaṅkūnnihanyāt | ardhaprādeśenārdhaprādeśenaikaikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet ||
4.d: अथोपरवाः प्रादेशमुखाः प्रादेशान्तरालाः । अरत्निमात्रं समचतुरश्रं विहृत्य स्रक्तिषु शङ्कून्निहन्यात् । अर्धप्रादेशेनार्धप्रादेशेनैकैकं मण्डलं परिलिखेत् ॥
4.m: Now the sounding-holes: their openings are a span [wide], and their intervals are a span. Having laid out a square of a cubit's measure, one should drive pegs into the corners. With half a span each, one should circumscribe each circle.
Leaving two strides from the eastern half of the sadas, the diameter of the hearth mounds is two spans; likewise their intervals.
The flank-measuring side of the fire-kindler's shed is five cubits.

4.s: etena mārjālīyo vyākhyātaḥ | tasyodīcīṃ dvāraṃ kurvanti ||
4.d: एतेन मार्जालीयो व्याख्यातः । तस्योदीचीं द्वारं कुर्वन्ति ॥
4.m: By this the mārjālīya shed is explained. They make its door facing north.

4.s: rathākṣāntarālā yūpāvaṭā bhavantītyekādaśinyāṃ vijñāyate | tasyā daśānāṃ ca rathākṣāṇāmekādaśānāṃ ca padānāmaṣṭāṅgulasya ca caturviṃśaṃ bhāgamādadīta | sa prakramaḥ syāt | tena vediṃ vimimīte ||
4.d: रथाक्षान्तराला यूपावटा भवन्तीत्येकादशिन्यां विज्ञायते । तस्या दशानां च रथाक्षाणामेकादशानां च पदानामष्टाङ्गुलस्य च चतुर्विंशं भागमाददीत । स प्रक्रमः स्यात् । तेन वेदिं विमिमीते ॥
4.m: The holes for the sacrificial posts are at intervals of a chariot-axle: thus it is known from tradition regarding the set of eleven posts. For it, one should take a twenty-fourth part of ten chariot-axles, eleven feet, and eight finger-breadths. That should be the stride. With that one measures out the altar.

4.s: athāśvamedhe viṃśatyāśca rathākṣāṇāmekaviṃśatyāśca padānāmaṣṭāṅgulasya ca caturviṃśaṃ bhāgamādadīta | sa prakramaḥ syāt | tena vediṃ vimimīte ||
4.d: अथाश्वमेधे विंशत्याश्च रथाक्षाणामेकविंशत्याश्च पदानामष्टाङ्गुलस्य च चतुर्विंशं भागमाददीत । स प्रक्रमः स्यात् । तेन वेदिं विमिमीते ॥
4.m: Now in the Aśvamedha, one should take a twenty-fourth part of twenty chariot-axles, twenty-one feet, and eight finger-breadths. That should be the stride. With that one measures out the altar.

4.s: atha prācyekādaśinyāṃ yūpārthaṃ vedeḥ pūrvārdhātpadārdhavyāsamapacchidya tatpurastātprāñcaṃ dadhyāt | nātrāṣṭāṅgulaṃ vidyate | na vyatiṣaṅgaḥ ||
4.d: अथ प्राच्येकादशिन्यां यूपार्थं वेदेः पूर्वार्धात्पदार्धव्यासमपच्छिद्य तत्पुरस्तात्प्राञ्चं दध्यात् । नात्राष्टाङ्गुलं विद्यते । न व्यतिषङ्गः ॥
4.m: Now in the eastern set of eleven posts, for the sake of the post, having cut off a strip of half a foot in width from the eastern half of the altar, one should place it eastwards in front. Here there is no eight finger-breadths; there is no overlapping.
The holes for the sacrificial posts have a diameter of a foot; the lower ends of the posts have a circumference of three feet.

5.s: ardhāṣṭamāḥ puruṣāḥ prathamo 'gniḥ | ardhanavamā dvitīyaḥ | ardhadaśamāstṛtīyaḥ | evamuttarottaro vidhābhyāsa ekaśatavidhāt | tadetatsaptavidhaprabhṛtyekaśatavidhāntam ||
5.d: अर्धाष्टमाः पुरुषाः प्रथमो ऽग्निः । अर्धनवमा द्वितीयः । अर्धदशमास्तृतीयः । एवमुत्तरोत्तरो विधाभ्यास एकशतविधात् । तदेतत्सप्तविधप्रभृत्येकशतविधान्तम् ॥
5.m: The first fire-altar is seven and a half men's heights; the second is eight and a half; the third is nine and a half. Thus the repeated addition of layers continues up to the hundred-and-one-fold. That goes from the sevenfold size up to the hundred-and-one-fold size.

5.s: ata ūrdhvamekaśatavidhāneva pratyādadīta | anagnikānvā yajñakratūnāharet | anyatrāśvamedhāt ||
5.d: अत ऊर्ध्वमेकशतविधानेव प्रत्याददीत । अनग्निकान्वा यज्ञक्रतूनाहरेत् । अन्यत्राश्वमेधात् ॥
5.m: Above that, one should repeatedly adopt only the hundred-and-one-fold; or else one should perform the sacrificial rites without a fire-altar, except for the Aśvamedha.
If one should undertake the Aśvamedha without having reached [the hundred-and-one-fold], one should multiply the form above this; one should not observe the other [rule].
If one should undertake it having passed [that limit], having undertaken it, one should repeat from the completed [measure] alone.
How indeed should one multiply the form?

5.s: yadanyatprakṛtestatpañcadaśa bhāgānkṛtvā vidhāyāṃ vidhāyāṃ dvau dvau bhāgau samasyet | tābhirardhāṣṭamābhiragniṃ cinuyāt ||
5.d: यदन्यत्प्रकृतेस्तत्पञ्चदश भागान्कृत्वा विधायां विधायां द्वौ द्वौ भागौ समस्येत् । ताभिरर्धाष्टमाभिरग्निं चिनुयात् ॥
5.m: Having made that which is other than the base model into fifteen parts, one should combine two parts in each form. With those seven and a half, one should pile the fire-altar.
Some teach the multiplication of the height measure by a twenty-fourth part of a fifth of the knee's height.
Now some pile [altars] beginning with the onefold size, without wings and tail.
That is not appropriate, because of contradiction between earlier and later [traditions].

5.s: atha haikeṣāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati śyenacidagnīnāṃ pūrvā tatiriti ||
5.d: अथ हैकेषां ब्राह्मणं भवति श्येनचिदग्नीनां पूर्वा ततिरिति ॥
5.m: Now there is a Brāhmaṇa passage of some: 'The falcon-shaped altar is the first arrangement of the fire-altars.'

5.s: athāpareṣāṃ na jyāyāṃsaṃ citvā kanīyāṃsaṃ cinvīteti ||
5.d: अथापरेषां न ज्यायांसं चित्वा कनीयांसं चिन्वीतेति ॥
5.m: Then of others: 'Having piled a larger [altar], one should not pile a smaller one.'

5.s: athāsmākaṃ | pakṣī bhavati | na hyapakṣaḥ patitumarhati | aratninā pakṣau drāghīyāṃsau bhavataḥ | tasmātpakṣapravayāṃsi vayāṃsi | vyāmamātrau pakṣau ca pucchaṃ ca bhavatīti ||
5.d: अथास्माकं । पक्षी भवति । न ह्यपक्षः पतितुमर्हति । अरत्निना पक्षौ द्राघीयांसौ भवतः । तस्मात्पक्षप्रवयांसि वयांसि । व्याममात्रौ पक्षौ च पुच्छं च भवतीति ॥
5.m: Now our [tradition is]: 'It is winged, for what is wingless cannot fly. By a cubit the two wings are longer; therefore winged are the birds. A fathom each are both wings and the tail.'

5.s: nāpakṣapucchaḥ śyeno vidyate | na cāsaptavidhasya pakṣapucchāni vidyante | na ca saptavidhaṃ citvaikavidhaprasaṅgaḥ | tasmātsaptavidha eva prathamo 'gniḥ ||
5.d: नापक्षपुच्छः श्येनो विद्यते । न चासप्तविधस्य पक्षपुच्छानि विद्यन्ते । न च सप्तविधं चित्वैकविधप्रसङ्गः । तस्मात्सप्तविध एव प्रथमो ऽग्निः ॥
5.m: A falcon without wings and tail does not exist; nor do wings and tail exist for one that is not sevenfold; nor after piling a sevenfold is there an occasion for a onefold. Therefore the very first fire-altar is only sevenfold.

5.s: bhedānvarjayet | adharottarayoḥ pārśvasaṃdhānaṃ bhedā ityupadiśanti | tadagnyanteṣu na vidyate na sraktipārśvayoḥ ||
5.d: भेदान्वर्जयेत् । अधरोत्तरयोः पार्श्वसंधानं भेदा इत्युपदिशन्ति । तदग्न्यन्तेषु न विद्यते न स्रक्तिपार्श्वयोः ॥
5.m: One should avoid breaks. They teach that breaks are the coincidence of joints between lower and upper [layers]. That does not occur at the fire-altar margins, nor at the sides of corners.
‘One piling for the first time should pile a thousand-[brick altar]’ [so the Brāhmaṇa says].
Or one should complete the number [of bricks] in the fifth layer.
If one wishes to make [layers] of two hundred [bricks each], one should understand an equal count with the five coḍā and the nākasad bricks.

6.s: paśudharmo ha vā agniḥ | yathā ha vai paśordakṣiṇeṣāmasthnāṃ yaddakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ taduttareṣāmuttaraṃ yaduttareṣāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ taddakṣiṇeṣāmuttaraṃ yadavāk cordhvaṃ ca tatsamānamevamiṣṭakānāṃ rūpāṇyupadadhyāt ||
6.d: पशुधर्मो ह वा अग्निः । यथा ह वै पशोर्दक्षिणेषामस्थ्नां यद्दक्षिणं पार्श्वं तदुत्तरेषामुत्तरं यदुत्तरेषां दक्षिणं तद्दक्षिणेषामुत्तरं यदवाक् चोर्ध्वं च तत्समानमेवमिष्टकानां रूपाण्युपदध्यात् ॥
6.m: The fire-altar indeed has the nature of an animal: just as in an animal's bones, what is the southern side of the southern [bones] is the northern [side] of the northern [bones], and what is the southern [side] of the northern [bones] is the northern [side] of the southern [bones], and what is below and above is the same, in this very way one should lay the faces of the bricks.

6.s: yā dakṣiṇāvṛto lekhāstā dakṣiṇata upadadhyāt savyāvṛta uttarataḥ | ṛjulekhāḥ paścācca purastācca bhavanti | tryālikhitā madhye | atha yā viśayasthā yathā ha vai paśoḥ pṛṣṭhavaṃśo naivaikasminpārśve vyatirekeṇa vartate naivāparasminnevaṃ tāsāmupadhānaṃ pratīyāt ||
6.d: या दक्षिणावृतो लेखास्ता दक्षिणत उपदध्यात् सव्यावृत उत्तरतः । ऋजुलेखाः पश्चाच्च पुरस्ताच्च भवन्ति । त्र्यालिखिता मध्ये । अथ या विशयस्था यथा ह वै पशोः पृष्ठवंशो नैवैकस्मिन्पार्श्वे व्यतिरेकेण वर्तते नैवापरस्मिन्नेवं तासामुपधानं प्रतीयात् ॥
6.m: One should lay lines turning to the right on the south side, and lines turning to the left on the north side. The straight-lined [bricks] are in the west and in the east; the triply inscribed [bricks are] in the middle. Now, those that lie in the middle axis—just as the backbone of an animal does not lean toward one side in preference nor toward the other, in that very manner one should understand their laying.

6.s: athāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati | prajāpatirvā atharvāgnireva dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇastasyeṣṭakā asthānīti ||
6.d: अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवति । प्रजापतिर्वा अथर्वाग्निरेव दध्यङ्ङाथर्वणस्तस्येष्टका अस्थानीति ॥
6.m: Moreover, there is a Brāhmaṇa [passage]: ‘Prajāpati is Atharvan; the fire-altar itself is Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa; its bricks are the bones.’
Therefore, if one piles beyond the body, one should connect from the middle of the body's overflow with the middles of the limbs' overflows.
‘Pile it facing east,’ so it is known [from scripture].
One should not complete the number [of bricks] with non-earthen [items] that are not bricks.
Because of this Brāhmaṇa [passage]: ‘One fire-altar is brick-piled, the other animal-piled.’

6.s: paśurvā eṣa yadagniryoniḥ khalu vā eṣā paśorvikriyate yatprācīnamaiṣṭākādyajuḥ kriyata iti ca ||
6.d: पशुर्वा एष यदग्निर्योनिः खलु वा एषा पशोर्विक्रियते यत्प्राचीनमैष्टाकाद्यजुः क्रियत इति च ॥
6.m: And because: ‘This fire-altar is indeed an animal; that womb of the animal is indeed altered which is made eastward from the brick-laying sacrificial formula.’
One should place space-filling objects into hollows.
One should recognize the marks on the bricks: a circle, an ox, a three-cornered sign.
When bricks exceed the formulas for the bricks, the lokaṃpṛṇā bricks are supplied, because of the absence of a fixed measure.
Or rather, one should lay here the groups of bricks already mentioned.
When the formula exceeds, one should place smeared pebbles into the joints.
‘He lays facing east, he lays facing west’: this is an instruction of direction within groups [of bricks].
‘He lays facing east, he lays facing west’: this is an instruction of the facing of the performer.
‘He lays some facing west in the east, and others facing east in the west’: this is the order of completion.

7.s: na khaṇḍāmupadadhyāt | na bhinnāmupadadhyāt | na kṛṣṇāmupadadhyāt | na jīrṇāmupadadhyāt | na lakṣmaṇāmupadadhyāt | na svayamātṛṇṇāṃ svayaṃcitāvupadadhyāt ||
7.d: न खण्डामुपदध्यात् । न भिन्नामुपदध्यात् । न कृष्णामुपदध्यात् । न जीर्णामुपदध्यात् । न लक्ष्मणामुपदध्यात् । न स्वयमातृण्णां स्वयंचितावुपदध्यात् ॥
7.m: One should not lay a broken brick; one should not lay a cracked brick; one should not lay a black brick; one should not lay a worn brick; one should not lay a marked brick; one should not lay a naturally perforated brick in one's own layer.

7.s: ūrdhvapramāṇamiṣṭakānāṃ jānoḥ pañcamena kārayet | ardhena nākasadāṃ pañcacoḍānāṃ ca ||
7.d: ऊर्ध्वप्रमाणमिष्टकानां जानोः पञ्चमेन कारयेत् । अर्धेन नाकसदां पञ्चचोडानां च ॥
7.m: One should make the upward measure of the bricks with the fifth part of a knee; with half [of that] for the nākasad and the pañcacoḍā [bricks].
Whatever is reduced by drying and baking, one should make up for that with loose earth filling, because the loose earth filling has no fixed measure.
‘It is extended-arm-span-sized,’ so it is known [from scripture] of the gārhapatya piling.
‘It is four-sided,’ according to some; ‘it is circular,’ according to others.

7.s: caturaśraṃ saptadhā vibhajya tiraścīṃ tredhā vibhajet | aparasminprastāra udīcīrupadadhāti ||
7.d: चतुरश्रं सप्तधा विभज्य तिरश्चीं त्रेधा विभजेत् । अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तार उदीचीरुपदधाति ॥
7.m: Having divided the four-sided [area] into seven parts, one should divide the transverse [line] into three. In the other layer, he lays [the bricks] facing north.

7.s: samacaturaśrāścedupadadhyādvyāyāmaṣaṣṭheneṣṭakāḥ kārayeccaturthena tṛtīyeneti | tāsāṃ nava prathamā dvādaśa dvitīyā iti pūrvasminprastāra upadadhāti | pañca tṛtīyāḥ ṣoḍaśa prathamā ityaparasmin ||
7.d: समचतुरश्राश्चेदुपदध्याद्व्यायामषष्ठेनेष्टकाः कारयेच्चतुर्थेन तृतीयेनेति । तासां नव प्रथमा द्वादश द्वितीया इति पूर्वस्मिन्प्रस्तार उपदधाति । पञ्च तृतीयाः षोडश प्रथमा इत्यपरस्मिन् ॥
7.m: If one lays equilateral four-sided figures, one should make the bricks with a sixth of an extended arm-span, a fourth, [and] a third. In the first layer he lays nine of the first [kind] and twelve of the second; five of the third [kind] and sixteen of the first in the second [layer].

7.s: parimaṇḍalāyāṃ yāvatsaṃbhavettāvatsamacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tannavadhā vibhajet pradhīṃstridhā tridheti | aparaṃ prastāraṃ tathopadadhyādyathā pradhyanīkeṣu sraktayo bhavanti ||
7.d: परिमण्डलायां यावत्संभवेत्तावत्समचतुरश्रं कृत्वा तन्नवधा विभजेत् प्रधींस्त्रिधा त्रिधेति । अपरं प्रस्तारं तथोपदध्याद्यथा प्रध्यनीकेषु स्रक्तयो भवन्ति ॥
7.m: In a circular [altar], having made an equilateral four-sided figure as large as possible, one should divide that into nine, [and] the segments into three and three. One should lay the second layer in such a way that the corners are at the junctions of the segments.
The dhiṣṇya hearths have a single layer, [and are] four-sided or circular.
Among them, having divided the āgnīdhra [hearth] into nine, one should lay a stone in place of one [brick].

7.s: atha hoturdhiṣṇyaṃ navadhā vibhajya pūrvāṃstribhāgānekaikaṃ dvedhā vibhajet ||
7.d: अथ होतुर्धिष्ण्यं नवधा विभज्य पूर्वांस्त्रिभागानेकैकं द्वेधा विभजेत् ॥
7.m: Then, having divided the Hotṛ's dhiṣṇya into nine, one should divide each of the eastern three parts into two.

7.s: athetarānnavadhā navadhā vibhajya madhyamapūrvau dvau bhāgau samasyet ||
7.d: अथेतरान्नवधा नवधा विभज्य मध्यमपूर्वौ द्वौ भागौ समस्येत् ॥
7.m: Then, having divided the others each into nine, one should unite the two central-eastern parts.

7.s: atha mārjālīyaṃ tredhā vibhajya pūrvāparau bhāgau pañcadhā vibhajet ||
7.d: अथ मार्जालीयं त्रेधा विभज्य पूर्वापरौ भागौ पञ्चधा विभजेत् ॥
7.m: Then, having divided the mārjālīya [hearth] into three, one should divide the eastern and western parts into five.
‘Mixing with the ash from the pan, one should make the bricks,’ [so it is said].
This applies only to one who has carried [the fire in the pot] for a year, not to one who carried it for [a few] nights.
Such is the formulaic arrangement of layers for this [altar].

7.s: chandaścitaṃ triṣāhasrasya parastāccinvīta kāmavivekāt tasya rūpaṃśyenākṛtirbhavatīti ||
7.d: छन्दश्चितं त्रिषाहस्रस्य परस्ताच्चिन्वीत कामविवेकात् तस्य रूपंश्येनाकृतिर्भवतीति ॥
7.m: Beyond the three-thousand-[brick altar] one should pile the chandaścit altar, according to the distinction of desires; its shape is hawk-formed.

8.s: atha vai bhavati śyenacitaṃ cinvīta suvargakāma iti ||
8.d: अथ वै भवति श्येनचितं चिन्वीत सुवर्गकाम इति ॥
8.m: Now indeed it is said: ‘One desiring heaven should pile a hawk-shaped altar.’
There is a twofold shape: with a four-sided body, and hawk-shaped.

8.s: pañca dakṣiṇāyāṃ śroṇyāmupadadhāti pañcottarasyām | basto vaya iti dakṣiṇeṃ 'sa upadadhāti | vṛṣṇirvaya ityuttare | vyāghro vaya iti dakṣiṇe pakṣa upadadhāti | siṃho vaya ityuttare puruṣo vaya iti madhya iti ca ||
8.d: पञ्च दक्षिणायां श्रोण्यामुपदधाति पञ्चोत्तरस्याम् । बस्तो वय इति दक्षिणें ऽस उपदधाति । वृष्णिर्वय इत्युत्तरे । व्याघ्रो वय इति दक्षिणे पक्ष उपदधाति । सिंहो वय इत्युत्तरे पुरुषो वय इति मध्य इति च ॥
8.m: ‘He lays five on the southern hip, five on the northern. He lays on the southern shoulder saying: “A goat is the bird”; on the northern saying: “A ram is the bird”. He lays on the southern wing saying: “A tiger is the bird”; on the northern saying: “A lion is the bird”; in the middle saying: “Man is the bird”.’

8.s: athāparaṃ vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyate yadagniriti | utpatatāṃ chāyayetyarthaḥ ||
8.d: अथापरं वयसां वा एष प्रतिमया चीयते यदग्निरिति । उत्पततां छाययेत्यर्थः ॥
8.m: And further: ‘This fire-altar is indeed piled in the likeness of birds’—that is to say, with the shadow of [birds] flying up.

8.s: samacaturaśrābhiragniṃ cinute daivyasya ca mānuṣasya ca vyāvṛttyā iti maitrāyaṇīyabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati ||
8.d: समचतुरश्राभिरग्निं चिनुते दैव्यस्य च मानुषस्य च व्यावृत्त्या इति मैत्रायणीयब्राह्मणं भवति ॥
8.m: ‘He piles the fire-altar with equilateral four-sided [bricks] to distinguish between the divine and the human,’ so runs the Maitrāyaṇīya Brāhmaṇa.

8.s: tasyeṣṭakāḥ kārayet puruṣasya caturthena pañcamena ṣaṣṭhena daśameneti ||
8.d: तस्येष्टकाः कारयेत् पुरुषस्य चतुर्थेन पञ्चमेन षष्ठेन दशमेनेति ॥
8.m: One should make bricks for it with a fourth, a fifth, a sixth, [and] a tenth of a man's height.

8.s: yāvānpuruṣa ūrdhvabāhustāvadantarāle veṇośchidre karoti | madhye tṛtīyaṃ | yadamutra spandyayā karoti tadiha veṇunā karoti ||
8.d: यावान्पुरुष ऊर्ध्वबाहुस्तावदन्तराले वेणोश्छिद्रे करोति । मध्ये तृतीयं । यदमुत्र स्पन्द्यया करोति तदिह वेणुना करोति ॥
8.m: He makes holes in a bamboo cane at an interval as large as a man with upstretched arms; a third in the middle. What one does elsewhere with a cord, that one does here with a bamboo cane.

8.s: tasyātmā samacaturaśraścatvāraḥ puruṣāḥ | pakṣaḥ samacaturaśraḥ puruṣaḥ | sa tu dakṣiṇato 'ratninā drāghīyān | etenottaraḥ pakṣo vyākhyātaḥ | pucchaḥ samacaturaśraḥ puruṣaḥ | tamavastātprādeśena vardhayet | evaṃ sāratni prādeśā saptavidhaḥ saṃpradyataḥ ||
8.d: तस्यात्मा समचतुरश्रश्चत्वारः पुरुषाः । पक्षः समचतुरश्रः पुरुषः । स तु दक्षिणतो ऽरत्निना द्राघीयान् । एतेनोत्तरः पक्षो व्याख्यातः । पुच्छः समचतुरश्रः पुरुषः । तमवस्तात्प्रादेशेन वर्धयेत् । एवं सारत्नि प्रादेशा सप्तविधः संप्रद्यतः ॥
8.m: Its body is an equilateral four-sided figure of four man's heights. The wing is an equilateral four-sided figure of a man's height; but on the south it is longer by a cubit. By this the northern wing is explained. The tail is an equilateral four-sided figure of a man's height; one should increase it at the rear by a span. Thus the sevenfold-sized [altar] is produced with the cubit and the span.

8.s: upadhāne pakṣāgrāduttarataḥ puruṣatṛtīyavelāyāṃ catasraḥ pañcamyastāsāmabhito dve dve pādeṣṭake tato 'ṣṭau caturthyaḥ | pakṣaśeṣaṃ ṣaḍbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | etenottaraḥ pakṣo vyākhyātaḥ ||
8.d: उपधाने पक्षाग्रादुत्तरतः पुरुषतृतीयवेलायां चतस्रः पञ्चम्यस्तासामभितो द्वे द्वे पादेष्टके ततो ऽष्टौ चतुर्थ्यः । पक्षशेषं षड्भागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । एतेनोत्तरः पक्षो व्याख्यातः ॥
8.m: In the laying: north of the wing-tip, at the line of one-third of a man's height, [there are] four fifth-part bricks, flanking them two quarter-bricks each, then eight fourth-part bricks. One should cover the remainder of the wing with sixth-part bricks. By this the northern wing is explained.

8.s: pūrvāparayoḥ pucchapārśvayoścaturbhāgīyā upadadhyāt | daikṣaṇottarayoḥ pādeṣṭakāḥ | śeṣamagniṃ pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet ||
8.d: पूर्वापरयोः पुच्छपार्श्वयोश्चतुर्भागीया उपदध्यात् । दैक्षणोत्तरयोः पादेष्टकाः । शेषमग्निं पञ्चमभागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् ॥
8.m: On the eastern and western flanks of the tail one should lay fourth-part bricks; on the southern and northern, quarter-bricks. One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fifth-part bricks.
This is a layer of two hundred [bricks].

8.s: aparasminprastāre pakṣāgrāduttarato 'rdhavyāyāmavelāyāṃ tisrastisraḥ ṣaṣṭhyo dve dve dvipade iti viparyāsamupadadhyāt | tathottare ||
8.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे पक्षाग्रादुत्तरतो ऽर्धव्यायामवेलायां तिस्रस्तिस्रः षष्ठ्यो द्वे द्वे द्विपदे इति विपर्यासमुपदध्यात् । तथोत्तरे ॥
8.m: In the other layer, one should place in alternation: north of the wing-tip, at a distance of half an extended arm-span, three sixth-part bricks, two two-foot bricks, [and so on]. Likewise on the northern [wing].
On the southern hip, nine sixth-part bricks made as squares; likewise on the northern [hip].

8.s: nava nava ṣaṣṭhyo dve dve dipade iti dakṣiṇādaṃsāduttarādaṃsādviparyāsamupadadhyāt ||
8.d: नव नव षष्ठ्यो द्वे द्वे दिपदे इति दक्षिणादंसादुत्तरादंसाद्विपर्यासमुपदध्यात् ॥
8.m: One should place in alternation from the southern shoulder and from the northern shoulder: nine sixth-part bricks each, two two-foot bricks each.
One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fifth-part bricks.

8.s: eṣa dviśataḥ prastāro vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādyāvataḥ prastārāṃścikīrṣet ||
8.d: एष द्विशतः प्रस्तारो व्यत्यासं चिनुयाद्यावतः प्रस्तारांश्चिकीर्षेत् ॥
8.m: This is a layer of two hundred [bricks]. One should pile in alternating arrangement for as many layers as one desires to make.

9.s: puruṣasya pañcamyaḥ | tā evaikato 'dhyardhāḥ | tāsāmardhyāḥ pādyāśca ||
9.d: पुरुषस्य पञ्चम्यः । ता एवैकतो ऽध्यर्धाः । तासामर्ध्याः पाद्याश्च ॥
9.m: Fifth-part bricks of a man's height; the very same, one and a half times [as long] on one side; half-bricks and quarter-bricks of these.
In the placement: on the eastern and western flanks of the wing, one should place half-bricks facing north; likewise on the northern [wing].

9.s: dakṣiṇottarayoḥ pucchapārśvayoścatasraścatasro 'dhyardhā udīcīḥ | pucchasyāvastāccatasro 'rdheṣṭakā udīcīḥ | tāsāmabhito dve pādeṣṭake | jaghanena pucchāpyayorekaikāmardheṣṭakāṃ prācīm ||
9.d: दक्षिणोत्तरयोः पुच्छपार्श्वयोश्चतस्रश्चतस्रो ऽध्यर्धा उदीचीः । पुच्छस्यावस्ताच्चतस्रो ऽर्धेष्टका उदीचीः । तासामभितो द्वे पादेष्टके । जघनेन पुच्छाप्ययोरेकैकामर्धेष्टकां प्राचीम् ॥
9.m: On the southern and northern flanks of the tail, four one-and-a-half-part bricks each, facing north; below the tail, four half-bricks facing north; on both sides of them, two quarter-bricks; to the rear, at the two joints of the tail, one half-brick each, facing east.
One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fifth-part bricks.
This is a layer of two hundred [bricks].

9.s: aparasmin prastāra ātmasraktiṣu catasraḥ pādeṣṭakā upadadhyāt | tāsāmabhito dve dve ardheṣṭake | pūrvasminnanike pañca ||
9.d: अपरस्मिन् प्रस्तार आत्मस्रक्तिषु चतस्रः पादेष्टका उपदध्यात् । तासामभितो द्वे द्वे अर्धेष्टके । पूर्वस्मिन्ननिके पञ्च ॥
9.m: In the other layer, one should place four quarter-bricks at the corners of the body; on both sides of them, two half-bricks each; on the eastern front edge, five.
At the two wing-tips, three one-and-a-half-part bricks each, facing north; in the intervals between them, one half-brick each, facing east.
One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fifth-part bricks.

9.s: eṣa dviśataḥ prastāro vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādyāvataḥ prastārāṃścikīrṣet ||
9.d: एष द्विशतः प्रस्तारो व्यत्यासं चिनुयाद्यावतः प्रस्तारांश्चिकीर्षेत् ॥
9.m: This is a layer of two hundred [bricks]. One should pile in alternating arrangement for as many layers as one desires to make.

10.s: atha vakrapakṣo vyastapucchaḥ ||
10.d: अथ वक्रपक्षो व्यस्तपुच्छः ॥
10.m: Now the curved-wing and spread-tail [altar].

10.s: tasyeṣṭakāḥ kārayetpuruṣasya caturthyaḥ | tāsāmardhyāḥ pādyāśca | nityamakṣṇyāpacchedanamanādeśe ||
10.d: तस्येष्टकाः कारयेत्पुरुषस्य चतुर्थ्यः । तासामर्ध्याः पाद्याश्च । नित्यमक्ष्ण्यापच्छेदनमनादेशे ॥
10.m: One should make bricks for it: fourth-part bricks of a man's height; half-bricks and quarter-bricks of these. Where not specified, the cut is always diagonal.

10.s: pādeṣṭakāścaturbhiḥ parigṛhṇīyādardhapadena padenādhyardhapadena padasaviśeṣeṇeti | te dve yathā dīrghasaṃśliṣṭe syātāṃ tathārdheṣṭakāṃ kārayet ||
10.d: पादेष्टकाश्चतुर्भिः परिगृह्णीयादर्धपदेन पदेनाध्यर्धपदेन पदसविशेषेणेति । ते द्वे यथा दीर्घसंश्लिष्टे स्यातां तथार्धेष्टकां कारयेत् ॥
10.m: One should enclose the quarter-bricks with four [sides]: by half a foot, by a foot, by one and a half feet, and by a foot increased by the specific excess. One should make a half-brick in such a way that two of those [quarter-bricks] are joined along their length.

10.s: athāgniṃ vimimīta | ātmā dvipuruṣāyāmo daśapadavyāsaḥ | tasya dakṣiṇādaṃsāduttarato 'dhyardhaprakrame lakṣaṇaṃ karoti | evamaparataḥ | tayorupariṣṭātspandyāṃ niyamyāṃsamapacchindyāt | etenetarāsāṃ sraktīnāmapacchedā vyākhyātāḥ | sa ātmā ||
10.d: अथाग्निं विमिमीत । आत्मा द्विपुरुषायामो दशपदव्यासः । तस्य दक्षिणादंसादुत्तरतो ऽध्यर्धप्रक्रमे लक्षणं करोति । एवमपरतः । तयोरुपरिष्टात्स्पन्द्यां नियम्यांसमपच्छिन्द्यात् । एतेनेतरासां स्रक्तीनामपच्छेदा व्याख्याताः । स आत्मा ॥
10.m: Now one measures out the fire-altar: the body has a length of two man's heights and a breadth of ten feet. One makes a mark one and a half strides north from its southern shoulder; likewise on the west. Having stretched a line over those two [marks], one should cut off the shoulder. By this, the cuts of the other corners are explained. That is the body.

10.s: śiro 'rdhaṣaṣṭhapadāyāmamardhapuruṣavyāsaṃ | tasyāṃsau prakrameṇa prakrameṇāpacchindyāt ||
10.d: शिरो ऽर्धषष्ठपदायाममर्धपुरुषव्यासं । तस्यांसौ प्रक्रमेण प्रक्रमेणापच्छिन्द्यात् ॥
10.m: The head has a length of five and a half feet and a breadth of half a man's height; one should cut off its two shoulders by a stride each.

10.s: pucchasya ṣaṭpadā prācī dvipuruṣodīcī | tasya pūrve srakti tribhistribhiḥ prakramairapacchindyāt ||
10.d: पुच्छस्य षट्पदा प्राची द्विपुरुषोदीची । तस्य पूर्वे स्रक्ति त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः प्रक्रमैरपच्छिन्द्यात् ॥
10.m: The tail has an eastward [length] of six feet and a northward [breadth] of two man's heights; one should cut off its two eastern corners by three strides each.

10.s: pakṣo dvādaśapadāyāmo daśapadavyāsaḥ | tasya madhyātprāñci ṣaṭpadāni prakramya śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt | śroṇyorekaikam | athainaṃ spandyayā paricinuyāt | antaspandyamapacchidya tatpurastāt prāñcaṃ dadhyāt | sa nirṇāmaḥ | etenottarasya pakṣasya nirṇāmo vyākhyātaḥ ||
10.d: पक्षो द्वादशपदायामो दशपदव्यासः । तस्य मध्यात्प्राञ्चि षट्पदानि प्रक्रम्य शङ्कुं निहन्यात् । श्रोण्योरेकैकम् । अथैनं स्पन्द्यया परिचिनुयात् । अन्तस्पन्द्यमपच्छिद्य तत्पुरस्तात् प्राञ्चं दध्यात् । स निर्णामः । एतेनोत्तरस्य पक्षस्य निर्णामो व्याख्यातः ॥
10.m: The wing has a length of twelve feet and a breadth of ten feet; having stepped off six feet eastward from its middle, one should drive in a peg; one at each of the two hips; then one should mark this out with a line; having cut off [the portion] inside the line, one should place it in front, extending eastward. That is the bending. By this, the bending of the northern wing is explained.

10.s: pakṣāgrayoḥ prakramapramāṇāni pañca pañca caturaśrāṇyanūcīnāni kṛtvā sarvāṇyavāñcamakṣṇayāpacchindyādardhānyuddharet ||
10.d: पक्षाग्रयोः प्रक्रमप्रमाणानि पञ्च पञ्च चतुरश्राण्यनूचीनानि कृत्वा सर्वाण्यवाञ्चमक्ष्णयापच्छिन्द्यादर्धान्युद्धरेत् ॥
10.m: Having made five squares each of stride-measure along the two wing-tips lengthwise, one should cut all of them diagonally southward and remove the halves.

10.s: evaṃ sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyataḥ ||
10.d: एवं सारत्निप्रादेशः सप्तविधः संपद्यतः ॥
10.m: Thus the sevenfold-sized altar with cubit and span is completed.

10.s: upadhāne śiraso 'pyaye caturthīmupadadhyāt | haṃsamukhī purastāt | pādeṣṭake abhitaḥ | tayoravastādabhitastisrastisraścaturaśrapādyāḥ | śeṣe pādeṣṭakāḥ ||
10.d: उपधाने शिरसो ऽप्यये चतुर्थीमुपदध्यात् । हंसमुखी पुरस्तात् । पादेष्टके अभितः । तयोरवस्तादभितस्तिस्रस्तिस्रश्चतुरश्रपाद्याः । शेषे पादेष्टकाः ॥
10.m: In the placement: at the joint of the head, one should place a fourth-part brick; a swan-beak brick in front; two quarter-bricks on either side; below and on either side of them, three square quarter-bricks each; on the remainder, quarter-bricks.

10.s: api vā śiraso 'gre haṃsamukhīmupadadhyāttasya avastāccaturthīmupadadhyātpādeṣṭake abhitaḥ | tayoravastādabhitastisrastisraścaturaśrapādyāḥ | śeṣe pādeṣṭakāḥ ||
10.d: अपि वा शिरसो ऽग्रे हंसमुखीमुपदध्यात्तस्य अवस्ताच्चतुर्थीमुपदध्यात्पादेष्टके अभितः । तयोरवस्तादभितस्तिस्रस्तिस्रश्चतुरश्रपाद्याः । शेषे पादेष्टकाः ॥
10.m: Or else, one should place a swan-beak brick at the tip of the head; below it, one should place a fourth-part brick; two quarter-bricks on either side; below and on either side of them, three square quarter-bricks each; on the remainder, quarter-bricks.

10.s: śiraso 'vastātpañcapādeṣṭakā vyatiṣaktā upadadhyāt | tathā pucchasya purastāt yadyadapacchinnaṃ tasminnardheṣṭakāḥ pādeṣṭakāścopadadhyāt ||
10.d: शिरसो ऽवस्तात्पञ्चपादेष्टका व्यतिषक्ता उपदध्यात् । तथा पुच्छस्य पुरस्तात् यद्यदपच्छिन्नं तस्मिन्नर्धेष्टकाः पादेष्टकाश्चोपदध्यात् ॥
10.m: Below the head, one should place five quarter-bricks interlocking; likewise in front of the tail; whatever was cut off, one should place half-bricks and quarter-bricks in that [space].

10.s: śeṣamagniṃ caturbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | pādyābhiḥ sārdhyābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
10.d: शेषमग्निं चतुर्भागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । पाद्याभिः सार्ध्याभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
10.m: One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fourth-part bricks; with quarter-bricks and half-bricks, one completes the count.

10.s: eṣa dviśataḥ prastāraḥ ||
10.d: एष द्विशतः प्रस्तारः ॥
10.m: This is a layer of two hundred [bricks].

10.s: aparasminprastāre haṃsamukhīścatasraścatasṛbhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhiḥ saṃyojayedyathā dīrghacaturaśraṃ saṃpadyate | tattiryak svayamātṛṇṇāvakāśa upadadhyāt ||
10.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे हंसमुखीश्चतस्रश्चतसृभिः पादेष्टकाभिः संयोजयेद्यथा दीर्घचतुरश्रं संपद्यते । तत्तिर्यक् स्वयमातृण्णावकाश उपदध्यात् ॥
10.m: In the other layer, one should combine four swan-beak bricks with four quarter-bricks so that an oblong is formed; one should place that transversely in the space of the naturally perforated brick.

10.s: haṃsamukhyau pratīcyau pucchāpyaye 'rdhapadenātmani viśaye | tayoravastādabhitastisraḥ pādeṣṭakāḥ prāṅmukhīrupadadhyāt ||
10.d: हंसमुख्यौ प्रतीच्यौ पुच्छाप्यये ऽर्धपदेनात्मनि विशये । तयोरवस्तादभितस्तिस्रः पादेष्टकाः प्राङ्मुखीरुपदध्यात् ॥
10.m: Two swan-beak bricks facing west at the joint of the tail, overlapping into the body by half a foot; below and on either side of them, one should place three quarter-bricks facing east.

10.s: pucchasyāvastātpañcadaśa pādeṣṭakā vyatiṣaktā upadadhyāt ||
10.d: पुच्छस्यावस्तात्पञ्चदश पादेष्टका व्यतिषक्ता उपदध्यात् ॥
10.m: Below the tail, one should place fifteen quarter-bricks interlocking.

10.s: pādeṣṭake ardheṣṭaketi pakṣapatrāṇāṃ prācīrvyatyāsaṃ cinuyāt ||
10.d: पादेष्टके अर्धेष्टकेति पक्षपत्राणां प्राचीर्व्यत्यासं चिनुयात् ॥
10.m: One should pile the wing-feathers eastward in alternating arrangement: quarter-bricks and half-bricks.

10.s: viśaye yadapacchinnaṃ tasminnardheṣṭakāḥ pādeṣṭakāścopadadhyāt ||
10.d: विशये यदपच्छिन्नं तस्मिन्नर्धेष्टकाः पादेष्टकाश्चोपदध्यात् ॥
10.m: In whatever was cut off at the junction, one should place half-bricks and quarter-bricks.

10.s: śeṣamagniṃ caturbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | pādyābhiḥ sārdhyābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
10.d: शेषमग्निं चतुर्भागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । पाद्याभिः सार्ध्याभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
10.m: One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with fourth-part bricks; with quarter-bricks and half-bricks, one completes the count.

11.s: puruṣasya pañcamībhiḥ śatamaśītiḥ saptārdhaṃ ca sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate ||
11.d: पुरुषस्य पञ्चमीभिः शतमशीतिः सप्तार्धं च सारत्निप्रादेशः सप्तविधः संपद्यते ॥
11.m: With fifth-part bricks of a man's height, one hundred and eighty-seven and a half, the sevenfold-sized altar with cubit and span is completed.

11.s: tāsāṃ pañcāśaddve cātmanyardhacaturthyaḥ śirasi | pañcadaśa pucche | aṣṭapañcāśatsārdhyā dakṣiṇe pakṣa upadadhyāt | tathottare ||
11.d: तासां पञ्चाशद्द्वे चात्मन्यर्धचतुर्थ्यः शिरसि । पञ्चदश पुच्छे । अष्टपञ्चाशत्सार्ध्या दक्षिणे पक्ष उपदध्यात् । तथोत्तरे ॥
11.m: Of them, fifty-two [are placed] in the body; three and a half in the head; fifteen in the tail; fifty-eight and a half one should place in the southern wing; likewise in the northern [wing].

11.s: ardhavyāyāmena sraktīnāmapacchedaḥ | saṃnataṃ pucchaṃ | pakṣayostribhistribhiraratnibhirapanāmaḥ | adhyardhyābhiḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ patrāṇi kuryāt | ākṛtiḥ śiraso nityā ||
11.d: अर्धव्यायामेन स्रक्तीनामपच्छेदः । संनतं पुच्छं । पक्षयोस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिररत्निभिरपनामः । अध्यर्ध्याभिः षट् षट् पत्राणि कुर्यात् । आकृतिः शिरसो नित्या ॥
11.m: The cutting of the corners is by half an extended arm-span; the tail is curved inward; the bend of the two wings is by three cubits each; one should make six feathers each with one-and-a-half-part bricks; the form of the head is constant.

11.s: puruṣasya pañcamyastā evaikato 'dhyardhāḥ | tā evaikataḥ sapādāḥ | pañcamabhāgīyāyāḥ pādyāḥ sārdhyāḥ | tathādhyardhāyāḥ | tayoścāṣṭamabhāgau tathā śleṣayedyathā tisraḥ sraktayo bhavanti | pañcamabhāgīyāyāścāṣṭamyaḥ | tāni daśa ||
11.d: पुरुषस्य पञ्चम्यस्ता एवैकतो ऽध्यर्धाः । ता एवैकतः सपादाः । पञ्चमभागीयायाः पाद्याः सार्ध्याः । तथाध्यर्धायाः । तयोश्चाष्टमभागौ तथा श्लेषयेद्यथा तिस्रः स्रक्तयो भवन्ति । पञ्चमभागीयायाश्चाष्टम्यः । तानि दश ॥
11.m: Fifth-part bricks of a man's height; the very same, one and a half times [as long] on one side; the very same, increased by a quarter on one side; quarter-bricks and half-bricks of a fifth-part brick; likewise of a one-and-a-half-part brick; and one should join eighth-parts of those two so that three corners are formed; and eighth-part bricks of a fifth-part brick; these are the ten [varieties].

11.s: ātmani pañcamabhāgīyāḥ sārdhyā upadadhyāt | tathā pucche ||
11.d: आत्मनि पञ्चमभागीयाः सार्ध्या उपदध्यात् । तथा पुच्छे ॥
11.m: One should place fifth-part bricks along with half-bricks in the body; likewise in the tail.
And one-and-a-half-part bricks along with half-bricks in the two wings.

11.s: aparasminprastāre pūrvayoḥ pakṣāpyayayorekaikāmubhayīmupadadhyāt | ekaikāmaparayoḥ | dve dve śirasaḥ pārśvayoḥ ||
11.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे पूर्वयोः पक्षाप्यययोरेकैकामुभयीमुपदध्यात् । एकैकामपरयोः । द्वे द्वे शिरसः पार्श्वयोः ॥
11.m: In the other layer, one should place one double brick at each of the two eastern wing-joints; one at each of the two western [wing-joints]; two on each of the two sides of the head.
Below the tail, one-and-a-half-part bricks facing east according to space; on the two flanks, quarter-bricks with eighth-parts.
And in the wings, one-and-a-half-part bricks along with fractional parts.
And one should lay down the remainder according to connection, according to number, and according to rule. || 11

12.m: By this, the body and the tail of the kite-shaped altar are explained. || 1
One should lay down five [bricks] in the head. Its form is explained. || 2
One should lay down fifty-seven in the southern wing; likewise in the northern. || 3

12.s: vyāyāmena saprādeśena pakṣayorapanāmaḥ | pañcamabhāgīyārdhyābhiḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ patrāṇi kuryāt | adhyardhāvaśiṣyate ||
12.d: व्यायामेन सप्रादेशेन पक्षयोरपनामः । पञ्चमभागीयार्ध्याभिः षट् षट् पत्राणि कुर्यात् । अध्यर्धावशिष्यते ॥
12.m: The bending of the two wings is by an extended arm-span with a span. With fifth-part half-bricks one should make six feathers on each side; one and a half bricks remain. || 4

12.s: tayā pucchasyāvastāt pādāvaratnimātrāvaratnyantarālau prādeśavyāsau bhavataḥ | tayoravastādabhito dvaudvāvaṣṭamabhāgau prāgbhedāvupadadhyāt ||
12.d: तया पुच्छस्यावस्तात् पादावरत्निमात्रावरत्न्यन्तरालौ प्रादेशव्यासौ भवतः । तयोरवस्तादभितो द्वौद्वावष्टमभागौ प्राग्भेदावुपदध्यात् ॥
12.m: Below the tail, by means of that [area], there are two feet, each one cubit in measure, separated by a cubit, and one span in width. Below them and on both sides, one should lay down two eighth-part bricks each, split eastward. || 5
Thus the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span is produced. || 6

12.s: atheṣṭakānāṃ vikārāḥ | pañcamabhāgīyāḥ sāvayavāḥ | pādeṣṭakāṃ caturbhiḥ parigṛhṇīyādardhaprādeśenādhyardhaprādeśena prādeśena prādeśasaviśeṣeneti | adhyardheṣṭakāṃ caturbhiḥ parigṛhṇīyādardhavyāyāmena dvābhyāmaratnibhyāmaratnisaviśeṣeneti | tāḥ ṣaṭ ||
12.d: अथेष्टकानां विकाराः । पञ्चमभागीयाः सावयवाः । पादेष्टकां चतुर्भिः परिगृह्णीयादर्धप्रादेशेनाध्यर्धप्रादेशेन प्रादेशेन प्रादेशसविशेषेनेति । अध्यर्धेष्टकां चतुर्भिः परिगृह्णीयादर्धव्यायामेन द्वाभ्यामरत्निभ्यामरत्निसविशेषेनेति । ताः षट् ॥
12.m: Now the modifications of the bricks: fifth-part bricks with subdivisions. One should encompass a quarter-brick by four [sides]: by half a span, by one and a half spans, by a span, and by a span increased by the specific excess. One should encompass a brick and a half by four [sides]: by half an extended arm-span, by two cubits, and by a cubit increased by the specific excess. These are six. || 7

12.s: tāsāṃ caturaśrapādyāḥ sāṣṭamabhāgāḥ pādayorupadhāya śeṣaṃ yathāyogaṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ yathādharmaṃ copadadhyāt ||
12.d: तासां चतुरश्रपाद्याः साष्टमभागाः पादयोरुपधाय शेषं यथायोगं यथासंख्यं यथाधर्मं चोपदध्यात् ॥
12.m: Having laid down square quarter-bricks with eighth parts of them at the feet, one should lay down the remainder according to connection, according to number, and according to rule. || 8 || || 12

13.s: alajacita etenātmā śiraḥ pucchaṃ ca vyākhyātaṃ pādāvapoddhṛtya ||
13.d: अलजचित एतेनात्मा शिरः पुच्छं च व्याख्यातं पादावपोद्धृत्य ॥
13.m: By this, the body, the head, and the tail of the alaja-bird altar are explained, excluding the feet. || 1
One should lay down sixty-three in the southern wing; likewise in the northern. || 2
The bending of the wings is by a man's height. || 3
Having measured a cubit eastwards from the western bend, and having fastened a cord to it, one should extend it to the other wing-feather boundary. || 4

13.s: evaṃ pañca pañcamyaḥ sārdhyā uddhṛtā bhavanti ||
13.d: एवं पञ्च पञ्चम्यः सार्ध्या उद्धृता भवन्ति ॥
13.m: Thus five fifth-part bricks with halves are removed. || 5

13.s: pādeṣṭakāmapanāma upadhyāya tāsāṃ caturaśra pādyāḥ sāṣṭamabhāgā apoddhṛtya śeṣaṃ yathāyogaṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ yathādharmaṃ copadadhyāt ||
13.d: पादेष्टकामपनाम उपध्याय तासां चतुरश्र पाद्याः साष्टमभागा अपोद्धृत्य शेषं यथायोगं यथासंख्यं यथाधर्मं चोपदध्यात् ॥
13.m: Having laid down a quarter-brick at the bend, and having removed their square quarter-bricks with eighth parts, one should lay down the remainder according to connection, according to number, and according to rule. || 6 || || 13

14.m: “One should pile the triangle-shaped altar” [so says the scripture]. || 1

14.s: yāvānagniḥ sāratniprādeśastāvatpraugaṃ kṛtvā tasyāparasyāḥ karaṇyā dvādaśeneṣṭakāstadardhavyāsāḥ kārayet | tāsāmardhyāḥ pādyāśca ||
14.d: यावानग्निः सारत्निप्रादेशस्तावत्प्रौगं कृत्वा तस्यापरस्याः करण्या द्वादशेनेष्टकास्तदर्धव्यासाः कारयेत् । तासामर्ध्याः पाद्याश्च ॥
14.m: Having made an equilateral triangle as large as the fire-altar with a cubit and a span, one should have bricks made with the twelfth part of its western producing side, their width being half of that; and halves and quarters of them. || 2

14.s: tāsāṃ dve ardheṣṭake bāhyasaviśeṣe cubuka upadadhyādardhyāścāntayoḥ ||
14.d: तासां द्वे अर्धेष्टके बाह्यसविशेषे चुबुक उपदध्यादर्ध्याश्चान्तयोः ॥
14.m: Of them, one should lay down two half-bricks with an outer specific excess at the chin, and halves at the two ends. || 3
One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with large bricks, [and] complete the count with half-bricks. || 4
In the other layer, one should lay down forty-seven quarter-bricks joined continuously in the western row. || 5
At the chin, [one should lay down] one pointed quarter-brick. || 6
And four oblong and other [bricks] one should lay down in the space of the naturally perforated brick, and halves at the two ends. || 7

14.s: śeṣamagniṃ bṛhatībhiḥ prācībhiḥ pracchādayedardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
14.d: शेषमग्निं बृहतीभिः प्राचीभिः प्रच्छादयेदर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
14.m: One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with large bricks directed eastwards, [and] complete the count with half-bricks. || 8 || || 14

15.m: “One should pile the rhombus-shaped altar” [so says the scripture]. || 1

15.s: yāvānagniḥ sāratniprādeśastāvadubhayataḥ praugaṃ kṛtvā navamena tiryaṅmānyāḥ praugacitoktā vikārāḥ ||
15.d: यावानग्निः सारत्निप्रादेशस्तावदुभयतः प्रौगं कृत्वा नवमेन तिर्यङ्मान्याः प्रौगचितोक्ता विकाराः ॥
15.m: Having made a rhombus as large as the fire-altar with a cubit and a span, the modifications stated for the triangle-shaped altar are [made] by the ninth part of the transverse-measuring side. || 2

15.s: aparasminprastāre cubukayorddhve pādeṣṭake upadadhyāt | saṃdhyantayośca dīrghapādye ||
15.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे चुबुकयोर्द्ध्वे पादेष्टके उपदध्यात् । संध्यन्तयोश्च दीर्घपाद्ये ॥
15.m: In the other layer, one should lay down two quarter-bricks at the two chins, and two oblong quarter-bricks at the two ends of the junction. || 4

15.s: dīrghe cetare ca catasraḥ svayamātṛṇṇāvakāśa upadadhyādardhyāścāntayoḥ ||
15.d: दीर्घे चेतरे च चतस्रः स्वयमातृण्णावकाश उपदध्यादर्ध्याश्चान्तयोः ॥
15.m: And four oblong and other [bricks] one should lay down in the space of the naturally perforated brick, and halves at the two ends. || 5

15.s: śeṣamagniṃ bṛhatībhiḥ prācībhiḥ pracchādayedardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
15.d: शेषमग्निं बृहतीभिः प्राचीभिः प्रच्छादयेदर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
15.m: One should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with large bricks directed eastwards, [and] complete the count with half-bricks. || 6 || || 15

16.m: It is known [from scripture]: “One should pile the chariot-wheel-shaped altar.” || 1

16.s: dvayāni tu khalu rathacakrāṇi bhavanti sārāṇi ca pradhiyuktāni ca | aviśeṣātte manyāmahe 'nyatarasyākṛtiriti ||
16.d: द्वयानि तु खलु रथचक्राणि भवन्ति साराणि च प्रधियुक्तानि च । अविशेषात्ते मन्यामहे ऽन्यतरस्याकृतिरिति ॥
16.m: Chariot wheels are indeed of two kinds: having spokes and having solid felloes. Because there is no specific distinction, we think: “[it may be] in the form of either.” || 2

16.s: athāgniṃ vimimīte | yāvānagniḥ sāratniprādeśastāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ parimaṇḍalāṃ kṛtvā tasminyāvatsaṃbhavettāvatsamacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya karaṇyā dvādaśeneṣṭakāḥ kārayet ||
16.d: अथाग्निं विमिमीते । यावानग्निः सारत्निप्रादेशस्तावतीं भूमिं परिमण्डलां कृत्वा तस्मिन्यावत्संभवेत्तावत्समचतुरश्रं कृत्वा तस्य करण्या द्वादशेनेष्टकाः कारयेत् ॥
16.m: Now he measures out the fire-altar. Having made the ground circular, as large as the fire-altar with a cubit and a span, and having made within it as large a square as can be accommodated, one should have bricks made with the twelfth part of its producing side. || 3
Having laid down six of them on the felloe, one should divide the remainder into eight parts. || 4

16.s: aparaṃ prastāraṃ tathopadadhyādyathā pradhyanīkeṣu sraktayo bhavanti ||
16.d: अपरं प्रस्तारं तथोपदध्याद्यथा प्रध्यनीकेषु स्रक्तयो भवन्ति ॥
16.m: One should lay down the other layer in such a way that the corners are in the rows of the felloe. || 5
One should have square bricks made with the fifteenth part of half a man's height for the purpose of measuring. || 7

16.s: tāsāṃ dve śate pañcaviṃśatiśca sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate ||
16.d: तासां द्वे शते पञ्चविंशतिश्च सारत्निप्रादेशः सप्तविधः संपद्यते ॥
16.m: Two hundred and twenty-five of them produce the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span. || 8

16.s: tāsvanyāścatuḥṣaṣṭimāvapet | tābhiḥ samacaturaśraṃ karoti | tasya ṣoḍaśeṣṭakā pārśvamānī bhavati | trayastriṃśadatiśiṣyante | tābhirantānsarvaśaḥ paricinuyāt ||
16.d: तास्वन्याश्चतुःषष्टिमावपेत् । ताभिः समचतुरश्रं करोति । तस्य षोडशेष्टका पार्श्वमानी भवति । त्रयस्त्रिंशदतिशिष्यन्ते । ताभिरन्तान्सर्वशः परिचिनुयात् ॥
16.m: Among them, one should add sixty-four others. With them, one makes a square; its flank-measuring side consists of sixteen bricks. Thirty-three remain over; with them one should pile around the borders on all sides. || 9

16.s: nābhiḥ ṣoḍaśa madhyamāḥ | catuḥṣaṣṭirarāścatuḥṣaṣṭirvediḥ | nemiḥ śeṣāḥ ||
16.d: नाभिः षोडश मध्यमाः । चतुःषष्टिरराश्चतुःषष्टिर्वेदिः । नेमिः शेषाः ॥
16.m: The hub is the sixteen middle [bricks]; sixty-four are the spokes; sixty-four are the altar base; the remainder is the rim. || 10

16.s: nābhimantataḥ parilikhet | nemimantataścāntarataśca parilikhya | neminābhyorantarālaṃ dvātriṃśaddhā vibhajya viparyāsaṃ bhāgānuddharet | evamāvāpa uddhṛto bhavati ||
16.d: नाभिमन्ततः परिलिखेत् । नेमिमन्ततश्चान्तरतश्च परिलिख्य । नेमिनाभ्योरन्तरालं द्वात्रिंशद्धा विभज्य विपर्यासं भागानुद्धरेत् । एवमावाप उद्धृतो भवति ॥
16.m: One should delineate the hub on the outside. Having delineated the rim on the outside and on the inside, and having divided the space between the rim and the hub into thirty-two parts, one should remove the portions alternately. Thus the addition is removed. || 11

16.s: nemiṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ kṛtvā vyavalikhya madhye parikṛṣet | tā aṣṭāviṃśatiśataṃ bhavanti ||
16.d: नेमिं चतुःषष्टिं कृत्वा व्यवलिख्य मध्ये परिकृषेत् । ता अष्टाविंशतिशतं भवन्ति ॥
16.m: Having made the rim into sixty-four, having inscribed it, one should draw [a circle] around in the middle. They become one hundred and twenty-eight. || 12
And one should divide the spokes into four each, and the hub into eight. || 13
In the other layer, one should draw around the hub on the outside at a fourth distance; the rim on the inside. || 15
Having made the rim into sixty-four on the inside, one should inscribe it. || 16
The division of the spokes is fivefold up to the two boundary circles. || 17
[One lays down] two each in the spaces on the rim, and one each in the spaces on the hub. || 18
Whatever is the remainder of the hub, one should divide that into eight parts. || 19
That is the chariot-wheel-shaped altar with spokes, having sixteen producing sides. || 20 || || 16

17.m: It is known [from scripture]: “One should pile the trough-shaped altar.” || 1

17.s: dvayāni tu khalu droṇāni bhavanti caturaśrāṇi ca parimaṇḍalāni ca | aviśeṣātte manyāmahe 'nyatarasyākṛtiriti ||
17.d: द्वयानि तु खलु द्रोणानि भवन्ति चतुरश्राणि च परिमण्डलानि च । अविशेषात्ते मन्यामहे ऽन्यतरस्याकृतिरिति ॥
17.m: Troughs are indeed of two kinds: four-sided and circular. Because there is no specific distinction, we think: “[it may be] in the form of either.” || 2

17.s: athāgniṃ vimimīte | caturaśra ātmā bhavati | tasya trayaḥ puruṣāstribhāgonāḥ parśvamānī ||
17.d: अथाग्निं विमिमीते । चतुरश्र आत्मा भवति । तस्य त्रयः पुरुषास्त्रिभागोनाः पर्श्वमानी ॥
17.m: Now he measures out the fire-altar. The body is four-sided; its flank-measuring side is three men's heights diminished by one-third. || 3

17.s: paścāttsarurbhavati | tasyārdhapuruṣo daśāṅgulāni ca prācī | tribhāgonaḥ puruṣa udīcīti ||
17.d: पश्चात्त्सरुर्भवति । तस्यार्धपुरुषो दशाङ्गुलानि च प्राची । त्रिभागोनः पुरुष उदीचीति ॥
17.m: The handle is at the back. Its eastward [measure] is half a man's height and ten finger-breadths; the northward is a man's height diminished by one-third. || 4
Thus the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span is produced. || 5

17.s: atheṣṭakānāṃ vikārāḥ | puruṣasya ṣaṣṭhyastā evaikato 'dhyardhāḥ | tāsāmardhyāstiryagbhedāḥ puruṣasya caturthya iti ||
17.d: अथेष्टकानां विकाराः । पुरुषस्य षष्ठ्यस्ता एवैकतो ऽध्यर्धाः । तासामर्ध्यास्तिर्यग्भेदाः पुरुषस्य चतुर्थ्य इति ॥
17.m: Now the modifications of the bricks: sixtieths of a man's height, [and] the very same ones increased by half on one side; halves of them split transversely; [and] fourths of a man's height. || 6

17.s: tāsāṃ tsaruśroṇyantarālayoḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṣṭīrupadhāya śeṣamagniṃ bṛhatībhiḥ pracchādayet | ardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
17.d: तासां त्सरुश्रोण्यन्तरालयोः षट् षष्टीरुपधाय शेषमग्निं बृहतीभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । अर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
17.m: Having laid down six sixtieths of them in the two spaces between the handle and the hips, one should cover the remainder of the fire-altar with large bricks; one should complete the count with half-bricks. || 7
In the other layer, one should lay down one and a half bricks directed northwards at the southern shoulder; likewise at the northern. || 8
In the eastern row, one should lay down sixth-part bricks. || 9
On the south and north [sides], [one should place] fourth-part bricks.

17.s: tsaroḥ purastātpārśvayorddhve caturbhāgīye upadadhyāt | tayoravastādabhito dve dve adhyardhe viṣūcī | tayoravastānmadhyadeśe dve ṣaṣṭhyau prācyau ||
17.d: त्सरोः पुरस्तात्पार्श्वयोर्द्ध्वे चतुर्भागीये उपदध्यात् । तयोरवस्तादभितो द्वे द्वे अध्यर्धे विषूची । तयोरवस्तान्मध्यदेशे द्वे षष्ठ्यौ प्राच्यौ ॥
17.m: In front of the handle, on its flanks, one should place two upright fourth-part bricks; below those two, on either side, two one-and-a-half-bricks facing away from each other; below those two, in the middle region, two sixth-part bricks facing east.

17.s: śeṣamagniṃ bṛhatībhiḥ prācībhiḥ pracchādayet | ardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
17.d: शेषमग्निं बृहतीभिः प्राचीभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । अर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
17.m: One should cover the rest of the fire-altar with large bricks facing east. One should complete the number with half-bricks.

18.m: With one hundred and twenty sixteenth-part bricks of a puruṣa, the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span is produced.
Having removed one of them, one makes the remainder into a circle.
That is explained by the earlier chariot-wheel-shaped altar.

18.s: ṣoḍaśīṃ purastādviśaya upadhāya tayā saha maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet ||
18.d: षोडशीं पुरस्ताद्विशय उपधाय तया सह मण्डलं परिलिखेत् ॥
18.m: Having placed a sixteenth-part brick in front in the interstice, one should draw the circle along with it.
What is cut off below, one should place in front.
The division of the fellies is into seven parts.
The central pieces of the felly have a width of one stride.
One should complete the number with half-bricks of the four-sided figures.
In the next layer, having placed a central felly piece at the lip, one should divide what is below into two parts.
That is the circular trough-shaped altar having nine producing parts.
The samūhya and paricāyya [altars] are explained by the earlier chariot-wheel-shaped altar.

18.s: samūhyasya dikṣu cātvālān khānayitvā tebhyaḥ purīṣaṃ samūhyopadadhyāt ||
18.d: समूह्यस्य दिक्षु चात्वालान् खानयित्वा तेभ्यः पुरीषं समूह्योपदध्यात् ॥
18.m: For the samūhya, having had pits dug in the cardinal directions, having swept together the loose earth from them, one should place it.
In the paricāyya, there is a variation of location for the bricks.
One should pile it round with all [the bricks] turning clockwise.

19.m: “One should pile the cemetery-mound altar,” thus it is known from sacred tradition.
Having divided the entire fire-altar into fifteen four-sided portions, the placement of these has been stated.

19.s: tribhirbhāgairbhāgārdhavyāsaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā madhyācchroṇī pratyālikhyāntāvuddharet | tasya daśadhā vibhāgaḥ ||
19.d: त्रिभिर्भागैर्भागार्धव्यासं दीर्घचतुरश्रं विहृत्य पूर्वस्याः करण्या मध्याच्छ्रोणी प्रत्यालिख्यान्तावुद्धरेत् । तस्य दशधा विभागः ॥
19.m: Having measured out with three portions a rectangle whose width is half a portion, having marked lines from the middle of the eastern producing side to the hips, one should remove the two ends. Its division is into ten parts.
Twenty of those make up the entire fire-altar.

19.s: aparasminprastāre praugamadhye 'nūcīnaṃ vibhajet | tasya ṣaḍdhā vibhāgaḥ | te dve parśvayorupadadhyāt ||
19.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे प्रौगमध्ये ऽनूचीनं विभजेत् । तस्य षड्धा विभागः । ते द्वे पर्श्वयोरुपदध्यात् ॥
19.m: In the next layer, one should divide along the axis in the middle of the triangle; its division is into six parts. One should place two of them on the flanks.
One should cause [bricks] to be made whose length is one-third of a portion and width is one-fourth. Half-bricks of these are formed by transverse division.

19.s: tā antayorupadhāya śeṣamagniṃ bṛhatībhiḥ prācībhiḥ pracchādayet | ardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
19.d: ता अन्तयोरुपधाय शेषमग्निं बृहतीभिः प्राचीभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । अर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
19.m: Having placed them at the two ends, one should cover the rest of the fire-altar with large bricks facing east. One should complete the number with half-bricks.
One should increase the upward height of the fire-altar by a fifth.

19.s: tatsarvaṃ tredhā vibhajya dvayorbhāgayoścaturthena vā navamena vā caturdaśena veṣṭakāḥ kārayet ||
19.d: तत्सर्वं त्रेधा विभज्य द्वयोर्भागयोश्चतुर्थेन वा नवमेन वा चतुर्दशेन वेष्टकाः कारयेत् ॥
19.m: Having divided all that into three parts, one should cause bricks to be made with a fourth, or a ninth, or a fourteenth of two parts.

19.s: tābhiścatasro vā nava vā caturdaśa vā citirupadhāya śeṣamavāñcamakṣṇayāpacchindyāt | ardhamuddharet ||
19.d: ताभिश्चतस्रो वा नव वा चतुर्दश वा चितिरुपधाय शेषमवाञ्चमक्ष्णयापच्छिन्द्यात् । अर्धमुद्धरेत् ॥
19.m: Having placed four, or nine, or fourteen layers with them, one should cut off the remainder obliquely downwards; one should remove half.
Its division is constant; the decrease or increase of the bricks is according to requirement.

20.s: kūrmacitaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta brahmalokamabhijayeyamiti | vijñāyate ||
20.d: कूर्मचितं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत ब्रह्मलोकमभिजयेयमिति । विज्ञायते ॥
20.m: “He who might desire: ‘May I win the world of Brahman,’ should pile the tortoise-shaped altar,” thus it is known from sacred tradition.

20.s: dvayāḥ khalu kūrmā bhavanti vakrāṅgāśca parimaṇḍalāśca | aviśeṣātte manyāmahe 'nyatarasyākṛtiriti ||
20.d: द्वयाः खलु कूर्मा भवन्ति वक्राङ्गाश्च परिमण्डलाश्च । अविशेषात्ते मन्यामहे ऽन्यतरस्याकृतिरिति ॥
20.m: Tortoises, indeed, are of two kinds: having curved limbs and circular. Since there is no distinction [in the injunction], we consider it to be the shape of either one.

20.s: athāgniṃ vimimīte | caturaśra ātmā bhavati | tasya daśa prakramāḥ pārśvamānī bhavati | tasya dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ prakramābhyāṃ sraktīnāmapacchedaḥ ||
20.d: अथाग्निं विमिमीते । चतुरश्र आत्मा भवति । तस्य दश प्रक्रमाः पार्श्वमानी भवति । तस्य द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां प्रक्रमाभ्यां स्रक्तीनामपच्छेदः ॥
20.m: Now he measures out the fire-altar: the body is a four-sided figure; its flank-measuring side is ten strides; the cutting-off of its corners is by two strides each.

20.s: pūrvasminnanīke prakramapramāṇāni catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā teṣāṃ ye antye te akṣṇayāpacchindyāt | evaṃ dakṣiṇata evaṃ paścādevamuttarataḥ | sa ātmā ||
20.d: पूर्वस्मिन्ननीके प्रक्रमप्रमाणानि चत्वारि चतुरश्राणि कृत्वा तेषां ये अन्त्ये ते अक्ष्णयापच्छिन्द्यात् । एवं दक्षिणत एवं पश्चादेवमुत्तरतः । स आत्मा ॥
20.m: Having made four four-sided figures measuring one stride in the eastern front, one should cut off diagonally those that are the ends. Thus on the south, thus in the west, thus on the north. That is the body.

20.s: śiraḥ pañcapadāyāmamardhapuruṣavyāsam | tasyāṃsau prakrameṇa prakrameṇāpacchindyāt ||
20.d: शिरः पञ्चपदायाममर्धपुरुषव्यासम् । तस्यांसौ प्रक्रमेण प्रक्रमेणापच्छिन्द्यात् ॥
20.m: The head has a length of five feet and a width of half a puruṣa; one should cut off its two shoulders by one stride each.

20.s: sraktyapacchede pādānunnayet | tasya dvipadākṣṇayā tiraścī taddviguṇāyāmamanūcī | tasya dvipadākṣṇayā pūrvamaṃsamapacchindyāt | etenetareṣāṃ pādānāmapacchedā vyākhyātāḥ | aparayoḥ pādayoraparāvaṃsāvapacchindyāt ||
20.d: स्रक्त्यपच्छेदे पादानुन्नयेत् । तस्य द्विपदाक्ष्णया तिरश्ची तद्द्विगुणायाममनूची । तस्य द्विपदाक्ष्णया पूर्वमंसमपच्छिन्द्यात् । एतेनेतरेषां पादानामपच्छेदा व्याख्याताः । अपरयोः पादयोरपरावंसावपच्छिन्द्यात् ॥
20.m: At the cutting-off of the corners, one should draw out the feet: the diagonal transverse [side] is two feet, and the axial [side] is twice that length; with the diagonal of two feet one should cut off its eastern shoulder. By this the cut-offs of the other feet are explained. For the two hind feet, one should cut off the two hind shoulders.

20.s: evaṃ sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate ||
20.d: एवं सारत्निप्रादेशः सप्तविधः संपद्यते ॥
20.m: Thus the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span is produced.

20.s: tasyeṣṭakāḥ kārayetpuruṣasya caturthyastāsāmardhyāḥ pādyāśca ||
20.d: तस्येष्टकाः कारयेत्पुरुषस्य चतुर्थ्यस्तासामर्ध्याः पाद्याश्च ॥
20.m: One should cause bricks to be made for it: fourths of a puruṣa, and their half-bricks and quarter-bricks.

20.s: adhyardhapādyāścaturbhiḥ parigṛhṇīyātprakrameṇa dvābhyāṃ padābhyāṃ padasaviśeṣeṇeti ||
