20.d: अध्यर्धपाद्याश्चतुर्भिः परिगृह्णीयात्प्रक्रमेण द्वाभ्यां पदाभ्यां पदसविशेषेणेति ॥
20.m: One should encompass one-and-a-half-foot bricks by four [sides]: by a stride, by two feet, and by a foot increased by the specific excess.

20.s: te dve yathā dīrghasaṃśliṣṭe syātāṃ tathaikāṃ kārayet ||
20.d: ते द्वे यथा दीर्घसंश्लिष्टे स्यातां तथैकां कारयेत् ॥
20.m: In such a way that two of them would be joined lengthwise, one should make one [brick].

20.s: dvipadākṣṇayārdhena samacaturaśrāmekāṃ ||
20.d: द्विपदाक्ष्णयार्धेन समचतुरश्रामेकां ॥
20.m: One [brick] is an equilateral four-sided figure [made] with half the diagonal of two feet.

20.s: upadhāne śiraso 'gre caturaśrāmupadadhyāt | haṃsamukhyāvavastāt ||
20.d: उपधाने शिरसो ऽग्रे चतुरश्रामुपदध्यात् । हंसमुख्याववस्तात् ॥
20.m: In laying down, one should place a four-sided brick at the tip of the head; below it, two swan-beak bricks.

20.s: pañca pañca caturaśrā dve dve pādeṣṭake iti pādeṣūpadadhyāt ||
20.d: पञ्च पञ्च चतुरश्रा द्वे द्वे पादेष्टके इति पादेषूपदध्यात् ॥
20.m: One should place on the feet five four-sided bricks and two quarter-bricks on each.

20.s: yadyadapacchinnaṃ tasminnardheṣṭakā upadadhyāt ||
20.d: यद्यदपच्छिन्नं तस्मिन्नर्धेष्टका उपदध्यात् ॥
20.m: In whatever is cut off, one should place half-bricks.

20.s: śeṣamagniṃ caturbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | ardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
20.d: शेषमग्निं चतुर्भागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । अर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
20.m: One should cover the rest of the fire-altar with fourth-part bricks. One should complete the number with half-bricks.

20.s: aparasminprastāre śiraso 'gre haṃsamukhīmupadadhyātpādeṣṭake abhitaḥ ||
20.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे शिरसो ऽग्रे हंसमुखीमुपदध्यात्पादेष्टके अभितः ॥
20.m: In the next layer, one should place a swan-beak brick at the tip of the head, and two quarter-bricks on either side.

20.s: tayoravastādabhito dve dve adhyardha pādye viṣūcī ||
20.d: तयोरवस्तादभितो द्वे द्वे अध्यर्ध पाद्ये विषूची ॥
20.m: Below those two, on either side, [one should place] two one-and-a-half-foot bricks facing away from each other.

20.s: tayoravastādabhitaśchedasaṃhite dve pādeṣṭake ||
20.d: तयोरवस्तादभितश्छेदसंहिते द्वे पादेष्टके ॥
20.m: Below those two, on either side, [one should place] two quarter-bricks joined to the cut.

20.s: dve dve dvipade tisrastisro 'rdheṣṭakā iti pādeṣūpadadhyāt ||
20.d: द्वे द्वे द्विपदे तिस्रस्तिस्रो ऽर्धेष्टका इति पादेषूपदध्यात् ॥
20.m: On the feet one should place two two-foot bricks and three half-bricks on each.

20.s: yadyadapacchinnaṃ tasminnardheṣṭakāḥ pādeṣṭakaścopadadhyāt ||
20.d: यद्यदपच्छिन्नं तस्मिन्नर्धेष्टकाः पादेष्टकश्चोपदध्यात् ॥
20.m: In whatever is cut off, one should place half-bricks and quarter-bricks.

20.s: śeṣamagniṃ caturbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | ardheṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet ||
20.d: शेषमग्निं चतुर्भागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । अर्धेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् ॥
20.m: One should cover the rest of the fire-altar with fourth-part bricks. One should complete the number with half-bricks.

21.m: With one hundred and twenty sixteenth-part bricks of a puruṣa, the sevenfold-sized altar with a cubit and a span is produced.

21.s: tāsāṃ pañca ṣoḍaśīrapoddhṛtya śeṣāḥ parimaṇḍalaṃ karoti | taduttareṇa droṇacitā vyākhyātam ||
21.d: तासां पञ्च षोडशीरपोद्धृत्य शेषाः परिमण्डलं करोति । तदुत्तरेण द्रोणचिता व्याख्यातम् ॥
21.m: Having removed five sixteenth-part bricks of them, one makes the remainder into a circle. That is explained by the following trough-shaped altar.

21.s: atha tāḥ pañca ṣoḍaśyastābhiravāntaradikṣu pādānunnayecchiraḥ purastāt | tāsāṃ parikarṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātam ||
21.d: अथ ताः पञ्च षोडश्यस्ताभिरवान्तरदिक्षु पादानुन्नयेच्छिरः पुरस्तात् । तासां परिकर्षणं व्याख्यातम् ॥
21.m: Then, with those five sixteenth-part bricks, one should draw out the feet in the intermediate directions, and the head in front. The drawing out of them is explained.

21.s: pradhīnāṃ saptadhā vibhāgaḥ pradhimadhyamāḥ prakramavyāsā bhavanti ||
21.d: प्रधीनां सप्तधा विभागः प्रधिमध्यमाः प्रक्रमव्यासा भवन्ति ॥
21.m: The division of the fellies is into seven parts; the central pieces of the felly have a width of one stride.
What turns out to be surplus should be combined with one-and-a-half-bricks of the four-sided figures.
In the next layer, the division of the feet is like that of the head, and that of the head is like that of the feet.
One should pile with alternating arrangement for however many layers one may wish to make.

21.s: kūrmasyānte tanu purīṣamupadadhyānmadhye bahulam | etadeva droṇe viparītam ||
21.d: कूर्मस्यान्ते तनु पुरीषमुपदध्यान्मध्ये बहुलम् । एतदेव द्रोणे विपरीतम् ॥
21.m: At the edge of the tortoise[-altar], one should place thin loose earth, and thick in the middle; this is precisely reversed in the trough[-altar].
Now indeed some declare the triangle-shaped and other altars beginning from the onefold-sized altar.

21.s: samacaturaśrāneka ācāryāḥ | tasya karaṇyā dvādaśeneṣṭakāḥ kārāyettāsāmardhyāḥ pādyāśca ||
21.d: समचतुरश्रानेक आचार्याः । तस्य करण्या द्वादशेनेष्टकाः कारायेत्तासामर्ध्याः पाद्याश्च ॥
21.m: Some teachers [prescribe] squares. He should have bricks made with a twelfth of its producing side, as well as half-bricks and quarter-bricks of these.
Now, for the fire-altar relating to the horse sacrifice, there is repetition of the man's height, not of the cubits and spans.

21.s: prākṛto vā triguṇaḥ | tristāvo 'gnirbhavatītyekaviṃśo 'gnirbhavatītyubhayaṃ brāhmaṇamubhayaṃ brāhmaṇam ||
21.d: प्राकृतो वा त्रिगुणः । त्रिस्तावो ऽग्निर्भवतीत्येकविंशो ऽग्निर्भवतीत्युभयं ब्राह्मणमुभयं ब्राह्मणम् ॥
21.m: Or the basic [fire-altar] tripled. "The fire-altar becomes three times as large," "the fire-altar becomes twenty-one-fold"—both are the Brāhmaṇa [statements]; both are the Brāhmaṇa [statements].
